title: Biostatistician / RWE Methodologist / Clinical Data Analyst
description:
### **About the company**

**What’s Promptly in a nutshell**

Promptly is building the first patient-centered global evidence network, offering real world data sharing and monetization capabilities. Together with a selected network of Partners, we generate new knowledge from harmonized datasets, augmented with the collection of longitudinal patient-reported data and patient-generated digital biomarkers within a secure and privacy-preserving environment.

We answer the question – is this patient treatment the best it could possibly be?

  
  

**What’s our purpose**

We exist to empower every patient and every health organization on the planet with evidence on the outcomes of care!

Why do we get up in the morning? Well, most healthcare professionals have chosen to work in healthcare driven by their desire to make a difference in patients’ lives. And so have we! We have chosen to follow this calling by addressing the biggest problem in healthcare: the lack of real-world evidence on the outcomes of care.

For us, society denying patients better care due to lack of access to data is unethical, in a world where technology improved so many aspects of our world. Making the right evidence available to healthcare organizations to help prevent one lost life, one care complication, one failed treatment is the moral obligation that big tech companies have – it’s our Hippocratic Oath.

At Promptly, everything we do is driven by our core purpose: to promote better healthcare at lower costs for patients every day, by making health outcomes available.

### **About the role**

Promptly runs real-world evidence (RWE) studies for pharmaceutical sponsors on routinely collected hospital data: electronic health records, laboratory results and clinical documentation from a federated network of partner hospitals. Some of these data are harmonised to a common data model such as the Observational Medical Outcomes Partnership (OMOP) model; others arrive in the hospital's own format. Patient-level data never leave a hospital. Analysis code runs inside each hospital's trusted research environment (TRE), and only aggregate results leave after statistical disclosure control (small-number suppression).

You are the statistician on these studies. You decide what a dataset can and cannot estimate, choose the design and the methods, quantify the uncertainty, and defend those choices to sponsors and clinicians. Everything we deliver has to stand up to methodological scrutiny, and you make sure it does.

You do not work alone. Clinicians at the partner hospitals and medical experts are your closest collaborators. Together you define outcomes and exposures that are clinically meaningful and measurable in routine data, and interpret what the results mean for patients. A Clinical Data Engineer builds the data pipelines and the analysis datasets you specify. Depending on your background, you may also derive cohorts and variables yourself from prepared extracts.

The team works in English. If you are early in your career, you will co-author your first protocols and statistical analysis plans (SAPs) with support from the RWE lead. You will grow into owning the statistical design and analysis of whole studies. If you are more experienced, you will own that from the start. The bar on statistical rigour is the same for both.

### **What you'll be expected to do**

* Turn clinical questions into study designs: estimand, target population and index date, comparator, confounding strategy, bias assessment, sample size and power.

* Work with clinicians and the sponsor's medical team to define outcomes, exposures and covariates. Check that what you measure in the data matches what they mean in practice.

* Specify the analysis dataset with the Clinical Data Engineer, or derive cohorts and variables yourself from prepared extracts in SQL and Python. Check data quality before analysis.

* Co-author protocols and SAPs with the RWE lead and clinical experts. The statistical parts are yours: estimands, analysis methods, sample size and how uncertainty is reported.

* Run the analysis in Python (or R): survival analysis (Kaplan-Meier, Cox, competing risks), propensity scores and multiple imputation, handling immortal-time bias and informative censoring. Derive inputs for health-economic models, such as transition probabilities.

* Prepare outputs that pass statistical disclosure control, then pool estimates across hospitals.

* Write the methods, statistical analysis and limitations sections of study reports, and present results to sponsors and clinical partners.

* Review sponsor protocols and concept sheets (short early study outlines), and say plainly what a proposed design can and cannot answer.

### **What we're looking for (qualifications & skills)**

You do not need to match every point. If you have a strong statistical foundation and want to learn the rest, please apply.

* An MSc or PhD in biostatistics, statistics, epidemiology or a related quantitative field, or equivalent applied experience.

* Strong foundations in statistical inference and observational study design: confounding, selection bias, and how to quantify and communicate uncertainty.

* Hands-on experience with time-to-event analysis, from a job, a thesis or a research project. Propensity scores, competing risks and multiple imputation are a plus, not a requirement.

* Python and SQL to a standard others can run, read and review. R is welcome but not required.

* Curiosity about the clinical side: you ask what a diagnosis code, a lab value or a visit means in practice before you model it. You enjoy working with clinicians.

* Written methods work you can point to: a protocol, an SAP, a paper or a thesis chapter.

* Clear English: you can explain a method and its limitations to a non-statistician, in writing and in meetings.

### **Preferred Qualifications**

* Experience with hospital or claims data, including clinical coding systems such as the International Classification of Diseases (ICD-10) or SNOMED CT.

* Familiarity with the OMOP common data model and the Observational Health Data Sciences and Informatics (OHDSI) tools.

* Experience with federated or distributed analysis, or with work inside a TRE.

* Experience with health-economic modelling or health technology assessment (HTA) submissions.

* Experience of discussing methods with pharmaceutical sponsors, clinicians or other external partners.

### **Position**

* Remote-first
* Full time
  

  

### **What we offer**

**Financial Benefits**

* Competitive salary
* Annual performance bonus
* Equity compensation via our ESOP (open to all team members)
* Annual training allowance
* Home-office equipment allowance
  

  

**Non-Financial Benefits**

* Equal opportunity and inclusive environment
* Flexible work schedule and vacation policy
* Corporate events and international team gatherings
  

  

### **What is the recruiting process like**

* There is a first interview with your future manager and/ or seasoned team members to get to know you and to give you an overview of Promptly and of the job you are applying to
* Afterwards, you will undergo a technical assessment stage, in which you will work on a test task or solve a business case.
* In same exceptional cases, a third interview might take place. Don’t worry if this happens. It’s because we have a good opinion on you, but there might be something we still need to get clear
* Finally, you will get your offer, and hopefully you’ll accept it!
* Also, we would like to notify you that during the final phases os the interview process, we may perform reference checks to validate the information provided in your application, resume, and discussed during the interview.

### **Our Culture & Values**

Empathy — Ownership — Responsibility — Teamwork — Excellence

If you embrace these values, you will thrive at Promptly. We are a purpose-driven company where everyone acts as an owner, committed to improving healthcare through data, technology, and collaboration.

The SKyRoCKeT Study will allow for a user-friendly, interpretable metric to more accurately inform public health/behavioral interventions, assessments, analyses, school-based health and physical education curricula and programs, and public health messages for young people and their caregivers.* To learn more about the study, please visit: **https://clinicaltrials.gov/ct2/show/NCT05770817**.

POSITION OBJECTIVE

Working under general supervision, the Data Science Researcher will support the Department of Materials Science and Engineering and the Solar Durability and Lifetime Extension Research Center by planning and conducting data-driven research activities related to materials durability, degradation science, and environmentally exposed technologies. This role will develop data analysis pipelines, perform statistical analysis, manage complex data structures and contribute to technical reports, progress summaries, and scientific manuscripts for submission to academic journals and conference proceedings. This is a one-year term-funded position expected to continue for one year contingent on project needs, funding availability, and satisfactory performance.

  

ESSENTIAL FUNCTIONS

* Conduct data science research to support Solar Durability and Lifetime Extension Research Center projects in materials durability, degradation science, and environmentally exposed technologies; develop and maintain data analysis pipelines, perform statistical and computational analyses, manage and create complex datasets, and present data using advanced statistical programming languages such as R and Python. (70%)

* Coordinate research activities with faculty, staff, and student researchers to support timely completion of project goals; track progress against project milestones, maintain research documentation, participate in project planning and team meetings, and assist with implementation planning efforts for events, workshops, symposia, or other programmatic requirements to implement research initiatives. (20%)

* Prepare and support dissemination of research products by conducting literature reviews, summarizing technical findings, contributing to technical reports, progress updates, presentations, posters, conference proceedings, and draft manuscripts, and ensuring research outputs are reviewed, documented, and released in accordance with project requirements and award guidelines (9%)

Perform other duties as assigned. (1%)

We are seeking a highly motivated computational scientist to join the Cardiovascular and Metabolic Disease (CVM) research organization at Biomedical
  
Research (BR) in Cambridge, MA. In this role, you will apply human genetics, statistical genetics, and genomic data science to support new therapeutic target discovery and patient selection strategies across CVM diseases.
  
The successful candidate will work closely with geneticists, computational biologists, disease-area scientists, translational researchers, and clinical development colleagues to generate actionable insights from human genetic and genomic data. This is an opportunity to contribute to innovative drug discovery programs and help advance genetically informed approaches to precision medicine.

### **About the Role**

**Key Responsibilities**

  
  

* Analyze and interpret whole exome/genome sequencing data to identify genetic variants, genes, and biological pathways associated with cardiovascular and metabolic diseases.
* Develop and apply statistical genetics and bioinformatics methods for variant annotation, association analysis, burden testing, rare-variant analysis, causal inference, and gene prioritization.
* Support the identification, evaluation, and validation of novel therapeutic targets using human genetic evidence and complementary genomic data sources.
* Contribute to patient selection and stratification strategies for research and clinical programs, including the identification of genetically defined patient subgroups.
* Integrate human genetics results with transcriptomic, proteomic, functional genomics, clinical, and other relevant data to develop disease and target insights.
* Collaborate with cross-functional project teams to define analytical strategies, interpret findings, and translate results into clear scientific recommendations.
* Develop reproducible, well-documented analytical workflows and contribute to best practices for genomic data analysis.
* Communicate results through presentations, written reports, scientific manuscripts, and internal project updates.
* Stay current with advances in human genetics, statistical genetics, genomic medicine, and computational methods relevant to drug discovery and development.
  

  

**Essential Requirements**

  
  

* PhD with 2-3+ years or MS with 6+ years of industry experience in human genetics, statistical genetics, computational biology, bioinformatics, epidemiology, biostatistics, or a related field.
* Postdoctoral research experience is preferred.
* Demonstrated experience analyzing whole exome/genome sequencing data, including variant quality control, annotation, filtering, association testing, and interpretation.
* Strong understanding of human genetics and statistical genetics principles, including rare-variant analysis and genotype-phenotype associations.
* Familiarity with genome-wide association studies, phenome-wide association studies, polygenic risk scores, Mendelian randomization, or functional genomics.

* Experience integrating genomic data with clinical, molecular, or multi-omic datasets.

* Programming and data analysis expertise in Python or R, along with proficiency in Linux or Unix-based computing environments.
* Knowledge of workflow management systems (Git), collaborative coding, and reproducible research practices.

* Strong scientific communication, collaboration, and problem-solving skills.

* Experience applying human genetic evidence to target discovery, target validation, or drug development.

title: ML Researcher
description:
**About the role**
------------------

Conduit is a frontier AI research company, training on a new modality of data: brain signals. Our first goal is to decode thought into text through a non-invasive headset. We're a team of about ten ML researchers and software engineers, working together in San Francisco.

Conduit's mission is to increase the communication bandwidth between humans and AIs—and to do so soon. We believe AGI is about to be a solved problem, but keeping humans empowered is not.

We have about 30,000 hours (and counting) of time-aligned brain signals and typing data, from about 1% of San Franciscans. Your job is to 1) train useful models given the data, and 2) steer our data collection operation so we get more useful data.

**What you'll do**
------------------

**Train models:** We're in a data-limited regime. As we scale up to 100x the amount of data we have now, we hope to also get 10-60x data efficiency wins. Research spans encoders, decoders, synthetic data, multimodal training, scaling laws, evals, post-training, and more.

**Steer data collection:** As we expand data operations, we want to track where our data collection can be improved. You'll be answering questions like: does sensor X or sensor Y lead to better downstream model performance? If we put the sensors on a dummy head that has known physical properties, do we see sensors performing as expected? Answering these questions involves physical experiments, statistical heuristics, and training many models.

**Optionally, a bit of everything:** We're a team of about ten. If you want to wear many hats – hardware, fundraising, recruiting, product – we welcome your efforts! If you prefer to focus solely on research, we welcome that too.

Your analyses will heavily rely on AI, and you'll have all the AI tokens you could want.

**Who you are**
---------------

Most important qualities:

* Brilliant and curious
* Deep and broad knowledge of ML
* Bonuses: undergrad-level physics and/or neuroscience intuitions

Example current employees include:

* Former lead of an AI alignment fellowship who studied physics and ML.
* PhD in ML architecture research with a B.A. in math, who questions everything from first principles.
* Top-5 college computer science dropout who joined a frontier AI company at age 21 and had previously interned at a top quant finance firm.

Our bar is a bit higher than the bar for researcher hiring at OpenAI/Anthropic/DeepMind, with the exception that we'll consider candidates with exceptional physics intuitions.

**Logistics**
-------------

* Location: San Francisco, fully in office
* Schedule: Full-time
* Benefits: Health, dental, and vision insurance. Free food for lunch, dinner, and whenever you're hungry. Personal trainer available. We pay for your commute.

**Application process**
-----------------------

Our process:

* A 30-minute call to get to know each other.
* A 2-hour coding assignment, where you're allowed to use AI.
* An hour-long chat about ML and the company.
* An approximately two-day work trial, where you'll do real tasks alongside us.
* Offer.

Description Manager, Data Scientist - Alternative Data Strategy

Data is at the center of everything we do. As a startup, we disrupted the credit card industry by individually personalizing every credit card offer using statistical modeling and the relational database, cutting edge technology in 1988! Fast-forward a few years, and this little innovation and our passion for data has skyrocketed us to a Fortune 200 company and a leader in the world of data-driven decision-making.

  
  

As a Data Scientist at Capital One, you’ll be part of a team that’s leading the next wave of disruption at a whole new scale, using the latest in computing and machine learning technologies and operating across billions of customer records to unlock the big opportunities that help everyday people save money, time and agony in their financial lives.

  
  

**Team Description**

The Alternative Data Strategy team drives credit decisioning forward by integrating non-traditional datasets into US Card strategies. As a Data Scientist, you will evaluate emerging vendors and data products, engineer high-impact features, build scalable processing and monitoring systems, and serve as the dedicated data domain expert guiding all users on dataset applications. In this role, you will also navigate risk governance for vendor models and build challenger models using new data to enhance existing ones. The scope involves rich cross-functional collaboration and continuous learning opportunities.

  
  

**Role Description**

**In this role, you will:**

* Partner with a cross-functional team of data scientists, software engineers, and product managers to deliver a product customers love
* Leverage a broad stack of technologies — Python, Conda, AWS, H2O, Spark, and more — to reveal the insights hidden within huge volumes of numeric and textual data
* Build machine learning models through all phases of development, from design through training, evaluation, validation, and implementation
* Flex your interpersonal skills to translate the complexity of your work into tangible business goals
* This role is designated as a hybrid position. You are expected to adhere to Capital One's hybrid policy regarding required on-site presence at your designated office location.
  

  

**The Ideal Candidate is:**

* Innovative. You continually research and evaluate emerging technologies. You stay current on published state-of-the-art methods, technologies, and applications and seek out opportunities to apply them.
* Creative. You thrive on bringing definition to big, undefined problems. You love asking questions and pushing hard to find answers. You’re not afraid to share a new idea.
* Technical. You’re comfortable with open-source languages and are passionate about developing further. You have hands-on experience developing data science solutions using open-source tools and cloud computing platforms.
* Statistically-minded. You’ve built models, validated them, and backtested them. You know how to interpret a confusion matrix or a ROC curve. You have experience with clustering, classification, sentiment analysis, time series, and deep learning.
* A data guru. “Big data” doesn’t faze you. You have the skills to retrieve, combine, and analyze data from a variety of sources and structures. You know understanding the data is often the key to great data science.
  

  

**Basic Qualifications:**

* Currently has, or is in the process of obtaining one of the following with an expectation that the required degree will be obtained on or before the scheduled start date:
  + A Bachelor's Degree in a quantitative field (Statistics, Economics, Operations Research, Analytics, Mathematics, Computer Science, or a related quantitative field) plus 6 years of experience performing data analytics
  + A Master's Degree in a quantitative field (Statistics, Economics, Operations Research, Analytics, Mathematics, Computer Science, or a related quantitative field) or an MBA with a quantitative concentration plus 4 years of experience performing data analytics
  + A PhD in a quantitative field (Statistics, Economics, Operations Research, Analytics, Mathematics, Computer Science, or a related quantitative field) plus 1 year of experience performing data analytics
* At least 1 year of experience leveraging open source programming languages for large scale data analysis
* At least 1 year of experience working with machine learning
* At least 1 year of experience utilizing relational databases
  

  

**Preferred Qualifications:**

* PhD in “STEM” field (Science, Technology, Engineering, or Mathematics) plus 3 years of experience in data analytics
* At least 1 year of experience working with AWS
* At least 4 years’ experience in Python, Scala, or R for large scale data analysis
* At least 4 years’ experience with machine learning
* At least 4 years’ experience with SQL

Description:

**This is a hybrid position requiring the team member to be onsite for 3 days per week.** **No relocation assistance is provided for this opportunity.**

  

**Who we are:**

At West, we’re a dedicated team that is connected by a purpose to improve patient lives that has been at the center of our Company for more than a century. Our story began when Herman O. West solved the problem of supplying penicillin in mass quantities to the US Government during World War 2. Through our work to deliver thousands of life-saving and life-enhancing injectable medicines to millions of patients daily, West’s indelible mark on the healthcare industry has just begun. A name started our story. How will yours help write our future?

  

There’s no better place to join an inclusive community of professionals with opportunities for lifelong learning, growth and development. Supported by benefit programs, we empower the physical, mental, emotional and financial health of our team members and their families.

  

We believe in giving back to help those in need in the communities where we live and work. And are equally committed to creating a healthier environment and planet through our sustainability efforts.

#### **Job Summary**

The Senior Associate, Data Science and Applied AI will develop AI methods and research applications at the intersection of materials science, biology and pharmaceutical drug containment and delivery.

Working with West’s R&D scientists, laboratory teams and AI engineers, this role will use machine learning, generative AI and scientific computing to accelerate materials characterization, experimental design, biological assessment and product development. The successful candidate will bring deep expertise in either materials science or biology, working knowledge of the other discipline, and demonstrated ability to apply AI to scientific problems.

**Essential Duties and Responsibilities**
-----------------------------------------

* Identify high-value research opportunities where AI can accelerate materials discovery, biological assessment, formulation, testing or product development.
* Develop machine-learning and statistical models using experimental, materials, biological, imaging and scientific-literature data.
* Apply AI to areas such as polymer and coating performance, structure–property relationships, material–drug interactions, biocompatibility, extractables and leachables, and degradation or stability.
* Build predictive models, scientific knowledge systems and decision-support tools for West scientists and engineers.
* Apply techniques such as active learning, Bayesian optimization, graph-based learning, computer vision, multimodal modeling and scientific foundation models.
* Use generative AI and agentic workflows to support literature review, patent analysis, hypothesis generation and research synthesis.
* Partner with laboratory scientists to design experiments that validate model predictions and generate higher-value datasets.
* Integrate structured laboratory data with scientific documents, images and other unstructured information.
* Quantify model accuracy, uncertainty, generalizability and scientific limitations.
* Develop reproducible code, data pipelines, evaluation methods and technical documentation.
* Translate research prototypes into usable tools in partnership with AI engineering, D&T, Quality and R&D teams.
* Communicate findings, assumptions and recommendations to scientific, technical and business stakeholders.
* Support intellectual-property development through invention disclosures, technical reports and patent-related analysis.
* Follow West requirements for data integrity, quality, information security, responsible AI and scientific rigor.

**Education**
-------------

* Bachelors degree in Materials Science, Polymer Science, Biology, Bioengineering, Computational Biology, Chemistry, Chemical Engineering or a related scientific discipline required, Masters degree preferred.

**Work Experience**
-------------------

* Minimum 3 years of relevant scientific research, applied AI or computational-modeling experience; doctoral research may be considered as relevant experience.
* Demonstrated experience applying AI, machine learning or advanced statistical methods to materials or biological research.
* Experience working with experimental scientists and translating scientific questions into computational approaches.

**Preferred Knowledge, Skills and Abilities**
---------------------------------------------

* Deep expertise in either materials science or biology, with sufficient knowledge to work across the interface between materials and biological systems.
* Strong proficiency in Python and scientific-computing libraries.
* Experience with PyTorch, TensorFlow, scikit-learn or comparable machine-learning frameworks.
* Knowledge of experimental design, statistical inference, uncertainty quantification and model validation.
* Experience with materials informatics, bioinformatics, computational biology, chemoinformatics or molecular modeling.
* Familiarity with polymeric materials, elastomers, coatings, surface science, drug–container interactions or biocompatibility.
* Experience analyzing spectroscopy, microscopy, mechanical-testing, molecular, assay or other laboratory datasets.
* Familiarity with large language models, scientific retrieval-augmented generation and knowledge graphs.
* Exposure to Azure AI Foundry, Azure Machine Learning, Azure OpenAI or comparable cloud platforms.
* Ability to distinguish scientifically supportable conclusions from exploratory model outputs.
* Strong technical writing, communication and cross-functional collaboration skills.
* Experience in pharmaceuticals, medical devices, combination products or regulated research environments preferred.
* Candidates are encouraged to provide publications, patents, research projects, code repositories or other evidence of interdisciplinary scientific and AI work. #LI-Hybrid #LI-MC1

-------------------------

Sedentary-Exerting up to 10lbs/4kgs of force occasionally, and/or negligible amount of force frequently or constantly to lift, carry, push, pull, or otherwise move objects, including the human body. Sedentary work involves sitting most of the time.

title: Sr. Data Analytics Manager
description:
Overview:

**ADVANCE YOUR CAREER. ADVANCE THE WORLD.**

At AMD, we believe technology has the power to solve the world’s most important challenges. From advancing healthcare and scientific discovery to powering AI and the technologies people rely on every day, innovation at AMD is shaping the future.

Whether you’re designing next-gen processors, enabling AI breakthroughs, or bringing leading edge products to market, every role at AMD contributes to something bigger — technology that moves the world forward. Join us and, together, we’ll advance your career.

Responsibilities:

**THE ROLE :**

AMD is seeking a Senior Manager of Marketing Data Science to build and scale data science capabilities within the Marketing Analytics team. This person will identify the highest-impact analytics opportunities across the full marketing funnel, translate them into actionable projects, and lead the work to deliver them. Part of this role will include building the data science capability from the ground up, developing and deepening relationships with stakeholders across Marketing, Product, and Sales Operations, and collaborating across teams to educate and influence the broader marketing organization on the effective use of data science. This person will own the marketing data science agenda, ensuring that data-driven insights are embedded in decision-making, campaigns and investments are continuously optimized, and marketing impact is more effectively measured and improved.

**THE PERSON :**

The ideal candidate is a strategic analytics leader and relationship-builder who thrives at the intersection of data science, marketing, and business decision-making, and who can help establish data science as a core capability across AMD Marketing. They must be able to translate complex business questions into actionable analytics projects, communicate technical insights in a clear and compelling way, and influence teams to use data more consistently in campaign planning, optimization, and investment decisions. They must also be a strong team player, able to build trusted relationships across Marketing, Product, Sales Operations, and technical teams while developing a new analytics capability from the ground up.

**KEY RESPONSIBILITIES:**

* Build and scale Marketing Data Science capabilities from the ground up, including the operating model, analytical frameworks, tools, processes, and governance required to support the broader marketing organization.
* Develop and own the Marketing Data Science roadmap**,** identifying and prioritizing high-impact analytics opportunities across the complete marketing funnel—from awareness and engagement through demand generation, pipeline, conversion, retention, and expansion.
* Measure and demonstrate the business impact of Marketing Data Science, establishing performance indicators and feedback loops that continuously improve models, campaigns, customer experiences, and marketing investments.
* Design and deliver advanced analytical solutions, including lead and account scoring, attribution, marketing mix modeling, experimentation, forecasting, segmentation, propensity modeling, and campaign optimization.
* Partner closely with Marketing, Product, Sales Operations, and other cross-functional stakeholders to understand business priorities, identify opportunities, and embed analytics into planning and decision-making processes.
* Ensure analytical solutions are scalable, reliable, and actionable, partnering with data engineering, technology, and platform teams to improve data quality, accessibility, integration, and model deployment.

**PREFERRED EXPERIENCE:**

### **Please see Special Instructions for more details.**

Employment in this role may be contingent upon extramural funding and successful performance and may be terminated or reduced in percentage of appointment if such funding is not secured or ceases to be available.

  

The Department of Medicine’s Center of Excellence on Digital Health Innovation conducts and supports quantitative and computational research across biomedical, clinical, and population health. This work provides the scientific and methodological foundation for the responsible design, development, validation, and deployment of artificial intelligence and machine learning solutions, including clinical algorithms and medical diagnostic tools intended to improve clinical research, care delivery, and patient outcomes.
  
  
In this role, you will serve as a core technical and scientific individual contributor, supporting the Center’s research and translational mission. You will design and execute rigorous analyses; advise on study design, data strategy, and analytical methods; assess data quality, representativeness, and limitations; and communicate findings in formats suitable for scholarly publications, grant applications, presentations, and translational decision-making.
  
  
The position requires strong scientific judgment, methodological rigor, and responsible stewardship of complex health data. You will work closely with investigators, clinicians, biostatisticians, epidemiologists, informaticians, engineers, and other collaborators to ensure that analytical approaches and AI-enabled solutions are scientifically valid, clinically relevant, and appropriate for their intended use.
  
  
**Key Responsibilities**  
  

* Lead or substantially contribute to the design and execution of quantitative analyses for biomedical and clinical research projects.
* Partner with investigators, clinicians, biostatisticians, epidemiologists, informaticians, and engineers to define scientific questions, analytic strategies, and study designs.

• Evaluate the suitability, completeness, structure, and limitations of data sources prior to analysis. • Prepare, clean, harmonize, and integrate structured and unstructured data from diverse biomedical and health system sources.
  

* Develop, implement, and validate statistical, predictive, and machine learning methods appropriate to the scientific question.
* Select analytical approaches that appropriately distinguish prediction, association, and causal inference.

• Evaluate model performance, calibration, robustness, generalizability, and clinical or scientific utility. • Identify and mitigate bias, confounding, missing data, measurement error, and data leakage. • Interpret results in context and communicate assumptions, uncertainty, limitations, and implications to scientific and clinical audiences.
  

* Produce manuscripts, abstracts, presentations, technical documentation, and analytical reports.
* Support reproducible research through version-controlled workflows, transparent documentation, and sound data management practices.
* Contribute to responsible data governance, including privacy, security, compliance, and ethical considerations.
* Advise collaborators on methodological choices and help determine when additional specialized expertise is warranted.
* Stay current with advances in biomedical informatics, machine learning, and responsible AI.

  
**Who Will Be Successful in This Role**  
  
The successful candidate will bring depth in one quantitative area, broad fluency across adjacent methodological domains, and the ability to work with substantial independence. Suitable backgrounds may include:

* A machine learning scientist with strong statistical and epidemiologic reasoning.
* A biostatistician or epidemiologist with advanced programming and applied modeling expertise.
* A biomedical informatician with experience leading data-intensive research efforts.
* A quantitative scientist with a record of translating complex data into publishable and actionable research.

The candidate should be able to set analytic direction, recognize when additional expertise is needed, and collaborate effectively with specialists across disciplines.

  

**Minimum Qualifications**

* Doctoral degree, or equivalent advanced training and experience, in biomedical informatics, data science, biostatistics, epidemiology, statistics, computer science, applied mathematics, engineering, public health, or a related quantitative field.
* Demonstrated record of independent or highly substantive contributions to biomedical, clinical, public health, or life sciences research.
* Advanced expertise in at least one primary quantitative area, such as:
  + Data science or machine learning o Biostatistics o Epidemiology o Biomedical or clinical informatics
  + Biostatistics
  + Epidemiology
  + Biomedical or clinical informatics
* Strong working knowledge of biostatistics and epidemiologic principles, including study design, statistical inference, bias, confounding, missing data, and interpretation of observational and experimental data.
* Proficiency in Python, R, or another statistical programming language.
* Proficiency in SQL and experience working with relational or analytical databases.
* Experience designing, implementing, and validating quantitative analyses using real-world biomedical data.
* Ability to evaluate model performance, calibration, and validity using methods appropriate to the research question and intended use.
* Demonstrated ability to communicate complex technical findings clearly to multidisciplinary scientific and clinical audiences.
* Experience producing reproducible analyses with clear documentation of methods, assumptions, and results.

  

**Preferred Qualifications**

* Experience leading or co-leading research projects in academic, clinical, or translational settings.
* Record of peer-reviewed publications, conference presentations, or grant-supported research.
* Experience with electronic health records, claims data, registries, clinical trials, genomic data, imaging data, sensor data, or other complex biomedical datasets.
* Experience with longitudinal data analysis, survival analysis, causal inference, or observational research.
* Experience developing or evaluating machine learning models in biomedical or clinical settings.
* Familiarity with natural language processing, large language models, or unstructured clinical text.
* Experience with cloud computing, distributed data platforms, or high-performance computing.
* Experience deploying analytical workflows, research tools, or decision-support systems.
* Familiarity with healthcare data standards and terminologies such as FHIR, ICD, SNOMED CT, LOINC, or OMOP.
* Knowledge of privacy, fairness, explainability, and responsible AI in healthcare.
* Experience mentoring trainees, junior analysts, or multidisciplinary collaborators.

description:
Description

**Location:** Indianapolis, IN Metro (Hybrid / 3-Day Onsite) *(Open to Regional/EST Candidates with Onsite Travel)*

About Xenon7

*Where elite tech talent meets world-class opportunities! At Xenon7, we work with leading enterprise clients and innovative startups on high-impact projects across Data, AI, Cloud, and Software Engineering. Our expertise in AI solution architecture and specialized technical talent allows us to partner with enterprise leaders on transformative initiatives, driving innovation and business growth.*

Role purpose

Lead the development and application of digital twins to improve clinical trial design and support evidence-based clinical development decisions. The role prioritizes digital-twin, simulation, and AI/ML expertise, supported by clinical-development experience and close partnership with trial-design experts.

Position overview

You will join a multidisciplinary clinical development environment and partner with clinical scientists, physicians, biostatisticians, pharmacometricians, biomarker experts, data scientists, data engineers, and other stakeholders. You will translate clinical development questions into quantitative strategies and deliver interpretable analyses that inform protocol design, patient selection, endpoint strategy, dosing, operational planning, and decision-making under uncertainty.

The role prioritizes digital twins as the primary capability for simulating patients, disease trajectories, treatment response, and clinical trials. The successful candidate will bring strong digital-twin, simulation, and AI/ML expertise, along with sufficient clinical-development knowledge to work effectively with trial teams. Deeper trial-design expertise can be developed through close collaboration with clinical scientists, biostatisticians, and pharmacometricians.

Key responsibilitiesDigital-twin development and validation

* Lead the design, development, and evaluation of digital twins of patients, disease trajectories, treatment response, or clinical trials using clinical trial and relevant external data.
* Combine mechanistic, statistical, causal, and machine learning approaches to create fit-for-purpose digital twins that can be simulated under alternative populations, interventions, dosing strategies, endpoints, or trial designs.
* Define use cases and contexts of use with clinical and quantitative experts so each digital twin addresses a specific trial-design or development decision.
* Assess calibration, validation, robustness, transportability, uncertainty, and practical relevance using appropriate internal and external evaluation strategies.
* Develop reproducible workflows and reusable digital-twin components that can be applied across programs or therapeutic areas.

Clinical trial design and quantitative decision support

* Partner with trial teams to frame development questions and evaluate design options, including target populations, eligibility criteria, enrichment strategies, comparators, endpoints, visit schedules, dosing strategies, and operational tradeoffs.
* Use digital twins and complementary simulation methods to compare plausible scenarios, characterize uncertainty, and support model-informed decision-making.
* Work closely with statisticians and pharmacometricians so analyses complement established trial-design methods and align with clinical and regulatory objectives.
* Communicate assumptions, limitations, and decision-relevant insights clearly to technical and non-technical stakeholders.

Data integration and scientific collaboration

* Analyze and integrate clinical trial data and, where relevant, biomarkers, imaging, digital health data, omics, patient-reported outcomes, and real-world data.
* Partner with data engineering and platform teams to create analysis-ready datasets, data-quality checks, lineage, and reproducible pipelines.
* Contribute to scientific documentation, presentations, publications, and responsible adoption of digital-twin methods across clinical development.

Model quality and responsible use

* Define the intended use, decision context, success criteria, and limitations of each model before development.
* Ensure models are interpretable, auditable, reproducible, and supported by evidence appropriate to their intended use.
* Apply appropriate governance, privacy, security, and scientific-review requirements for clinical data and analytical outputs.
* Clearly distinguish exploratory analyses from validated decision-support evidence and avoid overclaiming model capability.

 **Requirements**

* PhD in data science, statistics, biostatistics, pharmacometrics, computer science, biomedical informatics, engineering, mathematics, operations research, or a related quantitative field.
* Demonstrated experience developing digital twins, virtual patients, disease-progression models, clinical trial simulations, synthetic controls, or closely related computational models.
* Strong experience applying machine learning, statistical modeling, causal inference, or simulation to biomedical, healthcare, pharmaceutical, or other complex scientific data.
* Strong programming skills in Python, R, or a comparable analytical language, with experience using version-controlled and reproducible workflows.
* Sufficient clinical-development knowledge to frame relevant questions and collaborate effectively with clinical and quantitative trial experts.
* Ability and interest to deepen clinical trial-design knowledge through partnership with clinical scientists, biostatisticians, and pharmacometricians.
* Strong written and verbal communication skills and demonstrated effectiveness in cross-functional scientific collaboration.

Preferred qualifications

* Strongly preferred: experience supporting clinical trial design, protocol development, clinical development strategy, model-informed drug development, or regulatory-facing quantitative evidence.
* Familiarity with one or more trial-design topics, such as endpoint strategy, sample size or power assumptions, patient selection or enrichment, longitudinal outcomes, missing data, adaptive designs, or decision criteria.
* Knowledge of digital-twin architecture and validation, supported by expertise in causal inference, Bayesian modeling, survival analysis, longitudinal modeling, clinical trial simulation, or synthetic controls.
* Experience with clinical data standards and common clinical-development data sources.
* Experience with biomarker, imaging, omics, digital health, or real-world data and integration of multiple data modalities.
* Experience with scalable cloud-based analytical environments.
* Track record of translating analytical work into decisions, reusable capabilities, publications, presentations, or other measurable scientific impact.

Pure Earth is a growing international nonprofit addressing one of the most urgent yet solvable global health crises: toxic pollution and its profound impacts on human health. Pure Earth seeks a Data Scientist to strengthen our organization-wide monitoring, evaluation, and learning (MEL) systems during a period of significant growth. In this new role, reporting to the Director of MEL, you will be a hands-on analyst and advisor to headquarters (HQ) and country program teams: designing implementation research, analyzing and disseminating programmatic data, and turning findings into actionable programmatic or policy decisions.

You will work with researchers, program managers, and policymakers across multiple countries. You will analyze messy, real-world data, design implementation research protocols, and build statistical models that show whether and how our interventions work. Your findings will shape program strategy, inform government policy, and add to the global evidence-base on toxic pollution and health.

We are looking for someone who combines rigorous analytical and study-design skills with experience of large-scale public health programs, is comfortable with ambiguity, builds strong working relationships, and wants to help build new systems in a growing organization.

Hybrid New York City or remote

**Job Description:**

I. **Position Summary** :

Biomedical researcher with specialized training in quantitative methodology and a research focus on the biology of aging who:

  

* Manages, cleans, harmonizes, and analyzes complex data structures, including DNA methylation and other multi-omic aging biomarker data drawn from many independently collected cohorts.
* Constructs visualizations to depict trends and associations, conducts exploratory data analyses, and develops reports and summaries to communicate results to colleagues and scientific audiences.
* Works within a biomedical research team to facilitate the production of scientific work product (e.g. design and execution of studies or experiments, as well as publication and dissemination of findings), with particular strength in the development, benchmarking, and validation of epigenetic clocks and other aging biomarkers.
* Contributes to the scientific direction of projects by generating research questions, proposing study designs, and interpreting findings in their biological and clinical context.
* Develops and applies algorithms for summary and analysis of complex, multi-dataset data structures, including large-scale harmonization of heterogeneous biomedical datasets.
* Conducts statistical analysis for assessment of association and in service of causal inference.
* Participates in the design and development of custom software and reproducible analysis pipelines, including exploration of AI-agent-assisted data harmonization and foundation-model approaches, to facilitate analysis of biomedical research data and/or big data derived from research or administrative sources.
* Provides data analytic support to ongoing observational and interventional aging studies, and leads or participates in analyses of secondary data structures ranging from modest to very large size.
Contributes to funding applications and provides on-demand assistance with data analysis and interpretation.  

**II. Requirements:**

* Requires familiarity with statistical analysis, software development, visualization, algorithm development, supervised and unsupervised learning, and predictive analytics.
* Advanced skills in data management, manipulation, and summarization are critical, particularly for harmonizing DNA methylation and other omics datasets across multiple cohorts into standardized, reproducible analytic platforms.
* Skills in natural language processing and emerging AI-assisted data harmonization tools are a plus.
* Existing, or ability to develop, comfort with rigorous version control and the principles of reproducible research are required.
The ability to work in a team-based research environment is essential.  

**II. Core Competencies:**

* Ability to manage, manipulate and clean complex multi-omic data structures, including DNA methylation and other aging biomarker datasets drawn from multiple independent cohorts.
* Ability to conduct statistical, machine learning and predictive analyses including benchmarking and validation of aging biomarkers such as epigenetic clocks.
* Ability to formulate research questions and testable hypotheses in aging biology, and to design analyses that address them.
* Ability to write and publish peer-reviewed scientific manuscripts from analysis to submission and revision.
* Ability to organize analytic tasks and documentation files in a rigorous and reproducible fashion.
* Ability to develop exploratory analyses and analytic summaries in visual and written form.
* Ability to speak and present in English to communicate scientific results.
Ability to work collaboratively within multidisciplinary teams (scientific, IT and research operations), spanning fields such as geriatrics, genomics, and computational methods relevant to aging research.

* Generate analysis pipelines and automated functions for repetitive summaries and analyses.
* Develop and present reports of analytic findings. Lead or co-lead the development of abstracts and manuscripts, contribute to funding applications, and present findings internally and at scientific meetings.
Maintain current knowledge of the geroscience and biomarker literature and propose new analyses or research directions to the Investigators.

**Job Summary**

APPLY BY EMAIL ONLY - APPLICATION INSTRUCTIONS BELOW  
  
One full-time (40 hours/week) hybrid position is available. When applying, please indicate the track to which you are applying:  

* Computational Track (Ph.D. in a STEM discipline)
* Clinician-Scientist Track (M.D., Ph.D, or equivalent clinical degree)

  
Application Deadline: Applications will be reviewed on a rolling basis beginning October, 2026 and accepted until the position is filled.  
  
Anticipated Start Date: February, 2027 (flexible)  
  
Description  
The NEIL AND ELISE WALLACE STRATUS Center for Medical Simulation at BWH is committed to advancing medical education, patient safety, and healthcare outcomes through cutting-edge applications of medical simulation technologies supported by innovative curricula, contemporary educational methodologies, continuous improvement, and rigorous, multidisciplinary research.
  
At STRATUS, the Medical AI & Cognitive (MAICE) Lab, led by Dr. Roger Dias, MD, PhD, MBA, brings together a multidisciplinary team of clinicians, engineers, psychologists, computer scientists, and educators, including collaborations with several scientists and institutions, nationally and internationally. The core mission of our research lab involves the use of cutting-edge technologies to objectively measure and improve clinicians’ performance, with the ultimate goal of enhancing patient safety and improving clinical outcomes. Our projects have been funded by NASA, NIH, DoD, and NSF, leveraging machine learning and artificial intelligence to support high-performance clinical care in a variety of settings, including emergency medicine, critical care, surgery, space, and military medicine.  
  
The Postdoctoral Fellowship in Medical AI prepares the next generation of researchers to bridge artificial intelligence and clinical care. Building AI that clinicians trust and use requires both technical depth and clinical insight, so the fellowship is open to candidates from two backgrounds who work side by side in interdisciplinary teams:  
  

* Computational Track – for graduates of doctoral programs in Science, Technology, Engineering, and Mathematics (STEM) with a solid foundation in applying advanced ML/AI techniques. This track is ideal for early-career scientists seeking experience in the healthcare field and the opportunity to apply AI/ML and software engineering to improve patient care and safety. Prior experience in healthcare or biomedical research is required.
* Clinician-Scientist Track – for clinicians (M.D., D.O., PhD, or equivalent) with research experience and a strong interest in medical AI. This track is ideal for clinicians who want to lead the design, clinical validation, and implementation of AI tools while building hands-on data science and AI skills. This is a full-time research position with no clinical duties.

  
Fellows on both tracks are mentored by a multidisciplinary team of experts, gaining extensive knowledge and experience in diverse research areas including medicine, human factors, cognitive science, behavioral sciences, and aerospace and military research. Fellow follow an individualized development plan, with support for first-author publications, presentations at national and international conferences, and applications for independent fellowships and career development awards.  
  
Responsibilities  
All fellows will:  

* Conduct research and development in the emerging field of medical AI, from study design through publication, in settings such as emergency medicine, critical care, surgery, space, and military medicine
* Work with large multi-source clinical datasets, including time-series physiological data, demographics, behavioral and psychological assessments, video, audio, electronic health records (EHR), and clinical performance outcomes
* Contribute to the development and evaluation of AI-based medical simulation applications and real-time clinical decision support systems
* Lead first-author manuscripts and conference presentations, and contribute to grant proposals
* Collaborate closely with clinicians, engineers, and scientists, and help mentor students and junior team members

Computational Track fellows will focus on:  

* Designing and developing software architectures and data pipelines for AI-based solutions
* Training, fine-tuning, and evaluating ML/AI models, including neural networks, large language models, and computer vision models
* Integrating AI models with large clinical databases and deploying them in simulation and real-time clinical environments

Clinician-Scientist Track fellows will focus on:  

* Identifying clinically meaningful problems and translating them into AI research questions and study designs
* Designing and conducting simulation-based and clinical studies, including writing IRB protocols and leading data collection
* Defining clinical ground truth, including expert annotation of video, audio, physiological, and EHR data
* Evaluating AI systems, including large language models, for clinical accuracy, safety, bias, and usability, and studying how clinicians interact with AI tools
* Building hands-on skills in data analysis, programming, and AI through mentored projects and available training opportunities

**Qualifications**

title: Senior Research Scientist, AI & Workforce Intelligence - Remote, 4-Day Work Week
description:
**Work That Fits Your Life**

* **Fully remote, anywhere in the U.S.** We're headquartered in Chicago, but your office is wherever you do your best work.
* **A four-day workweek.** Work-life balance is built into our business, with a full-time, 32-hour week over four days.
* **Time to recharge.** You'll get generous PTO, paid holidays, and a paid company shutdown from December 24 through January 1.
* **Benefits for you and your family.** We offer medical, dental, and vision coverage, a 401(k) with company matching, and 12 weeks of paid new parent leave.

**What Sets Us Apart: We Value Every Job**

You don't have to be a scientist to be part of the science. Every job here, from sales and marketing to product and engineering, helps turn that science into better talent insights for our customers.

* **Our Mission.** Wonderlic's mission is to create a world where everyone finds and thrives in their best job.
* **Scientific Excellence.** We pair nearly 90 years of assessment science with industrial-organizational (I-O) psychology, machine learning, and AI.
* **What Our Work Makes Possible.** Our tools help HR teams spot great candidates, see who's most likely to succeed on the job, develop their people, and build stronger teams.
* **We Practice What We Sell.** We help companies hire and develop the right people, and we use the same approach to build and grow our own team. You're hired for your potential, and we help you develop it.

**Overview:**
-------------

Wonderlic is seeking a Senior Research Scientist to sit at the precise intersection of I-O psychology and machine learning - someone who has spent time building real systems with real data who cares deeply about what those systems are predicting. This is not a role for an ML engineer who finds people data interesting as a side project, or for an I-O psychologist who has learned to code. We're looking for someone who has genuinely lived in both worlds and is ready to own the problems that live between them.

Wonderlic built its applied AI/ML team from scratch, developed the Jobs Engine, a first-of-its-kind machine learning system for job analysis at scale, and won the 2025 SIOP Machine Learning Competition. We're now refining and expanding that work to deliver sharper, richer job analysis insights across thousands of roles. You will own the continued improvement of our jobs engine, the system that ingests labor market data and produces job analysis at scale across thousands of roles, and serve as one of the organization's experts on how AI should be applied to both employee selection and development.

**Your Impact:**
----------------

As Senior Research Scientist, you will set the scientific and technical direction for how Wonderlic understands work at scale and translates assessment science into AI-powered insight. Your work will directly determine the quality, defensibility, and reach of the inferences our platform makes about jobs and people - inferences that drive hiring decisions, development plans, and coaching conversations for millions of users. You will be the person in the organization who can hold both the I-O science question and the production ML question in the same breath, and answer both.

**What You'll Do**
------------------

**Lead the Continued Development of the Jobs Engine:** Own the architecture, integrity, and continuous expansion of Wonderlic's AI job analysis system, which ingests labor market data from O\*NET, LinkedIn, Indeed, and other sources to extrapolate cognitive complexity ratings, norm groups, and occupational interest profiles for thousands of jobs. Build and refine the models that make inferences about work content from unstructured text. Leverage existing occupational taxonomies (e.g., O\*NET, ESCO) where appropriate but also expand beyond them. Ensure all outputs are scientifically defensible and scalable as the nature of work evolves.

**Act as an Expert on AI Implementation Across the Organization:** Partner with product managers, engineers, and I-O psychologists to translate scientific requirements into AI-powered systems and ensure those systems meet the standards the work demands. Advise on which approaches are best suited to specific implementation challenges - assessment interpretation, manager and teams reporting, coaching content - and help teams understand what good looks like before they build and after they ship. Serve as an internal resource on what ML and AI can and cannot do in assessment and organizational contexts, and contribute to Wonderlic's external scientific credibility.

**Drive Scientific Rigor:** Apply I-O psychology principles - adverse impact consideration, norm group construction, and evidence-based evaluation standards - to every system you build. Ensure that Wonderlic's AI products meet professional and legal standards for selection and development tools. Push back when speed is being prioritized at the expense of defensibility, and find pragmatic paths forward when theoretical purity would prevent shipping.

**What Success Looks Like:** In your first six months, you will have a deep understanding of the jobs engine architecture and shipped at least one meaningful improvement to its coverage, accuracy, or scientific defensibility. You will have established working  
relationships with the I-O and Product teams and have a clear roadmap for the continued integration of AI into the platform.

Within a year, you will have materially expanded the jobs engine's reach and accuracy with demonstrable improvements to its coverage and the quality of inferences it produces. You will have contributed to the continued integration of AI across the platform, and be the person your colleagues go to with the hardest ML-meets-IO-science problems - not because you have every answer, but because you know how to find them.

The long-term marker of success is a jobs engine that provides defensible, scaled job analysis inference across millions of roles using a wide variety of inputs, AI capabilities integrated into the platform in ways that hold up to scientific and professional scrutiny, and a track record of using these technologies to improve people's understanding of themselves, their work, and their teams. You will also have helped to develop new assessments that leverage emerging technologies which allow for richer and more secure evaluation of individuals.

**What We're Looking For:**
---------------------------

**Skills & Capabilities:**

* **Applied NLP and ML engineering skills:** embeddings, semantic search, clustering, text classification, transformer architectures, model tuning and evaluation, all on potentially messy, unstructured data
* **Occupational data modeling:** job titles, task statements, skills, competencies, credentials, job families, seniority levels, title normalization, job similarity, role differentiation, and occupational frameworks such as O\*NET and ESCO
* **Responsible AI judgment in employment contexts:** fairness, explainability, auditability, bias mitigation, human review, and legal and ethical considerations in AI-supported selection and employee development systems
* **Generative AI evaluation skills:** rubric-based review, groundedness checks, error analysis, regression testing, and evaluation of LLM-generated job descriptions, work-context summaries, and assessment result contextualization.
* **Product judgment for applied ML systems:** balancing accuracy, explainability, automation, expert review, user input, maintainability, uncertainty, and job-specific nuance.
* **Working fluency with assessment and I/O concepts:** job relatedness, criterion relationships, adverse impact, norm groups, assessment profiles, and score interpretation.
* **Ability to own ambiguous, high-complexity problems:** framing underspecified problems, challenging weak assumptions, learning domain constraints quickly, and driving durable solutions in a small-company environment.

**Mindset:**

* You came to I-O psychology because you care about work - what makes it meaningful, who thrives in it, how to measure fit. That hasn't changed.
* You have a healthy relationship with "good enough": you know that perfect is the enemy of shipped, and you have the judgment to know where the line is.
* You can hold both worlds simultaneously: what does this score mean for a real person, and how do I build the system that generates it.
* You are genuinely curious about the problems that exist for both employee selection and development, not just tolerant of them.
* You thrive in an environment that requires creativity and scrappiness: you can work comfortably in a situation where the problems are hard, the team is small, the constraints are many, and the ownership is real.

**Qualifications**
------------------

* Graduate degree in I-O Psychology, Organizational Psychology, Organizational Development, or closely related field (quantitative focus strongly preferred); doctoral degree a plus
* Demonstrated ML engineering experience with shipped, production-grade systems - not just research or coursework
* Experience applying modern NLP methods to behavioral, assessment-based, or labor market data
* Track record of work that had to be both technically sound and legally/professionally defensible
* Minimum 3 years of applied industry experience; 5+ years preferred
* Experience at the intersection of I-O science and algorithmic fairness strongly preferred
* Familiarity with occupational taxonomies, vocational interests, or cognitive ability frameworks a significant plus

  

**Compensation:**

* $130,000 to $150,000 based on experience and expertise.

**Our Policy**
--------------

Affirmative Action Plan/Equal Employer Opportunity (AAP/EEO) Statement: Research suggests that both the confidence gap and imposter syndrome can make members of some groups (including women, members of the LGBTQIA+ and BIPOC communities, and candidates of less traditional age, education, or background) less likely to apply for jobs when they don't meet 100% of the qualifications. At Wonderlic, we are in the business of identifying potential, and we encourage all interested candidates to apply.

Wonderlic is proud to be an equal employment opportunity/affirmative action employer. Here, diversity is valued and celebrated, and this is what makes us such a successful team. Wonderlic does not discriminate in employment on the basis of race, color, religion, gender, gender identity, pregnancy status, national origin, sexual orientation, marital status, disability, genetic information, age, parental status, military/veteran status, or any other factor protected by law.

In addition, we will ensure that individuals with disabilities are provided reasonable accommodation to participate in the job application or interview process, perform essential job functions, and receive other benefits and privileges of employment. Please get in touch with us at jobs@wonderlic.com to request an accommodation.

title: Senior Data Scientist, AI
description:
**JOB SUMMARY**
---------------

* The Senior Data Scientist, AI executes data science, machine learning, statistical modeling, generative AI, agentic AI, evaluation, and advanced analytics work required to power BSWH’s priority AI use cases and workflow-enabled solutions.
* This role partners closely with AI Product Managers, Data Product Managers, AI Engineers, Software Engineering, Ontology and Knowledge teams, Quality Engineering, Clinical, Operations, Digital, Journey, Privacy, Security, and Governance stakeholders to translate business and clinical questions into rigorous data science solutions.
* The role develops predictive and statistical models, LLM- and agent-based capabilities, analytical frameworks, evaluation approaches, outcome measures, and reusable AI/data science assets that help AI-enabled products improve customer experience, operational efficiency, clinical workflows, personalization, decision support, and enterprise performance.
* This role is expected to combine strong statistical and machine learning skills with hands-on generative AI and agent engineering capabilities, practical product judgment, healthcare data fluency, and the ability to translate ambiguous problems into deployed solutions that work in real operational workflows.
* The Senior Data Scientist, AI reports to the Vice President, Data Science and may operate as either a senior individual contributor or a small-team technical lead, depending on assigned domain and portfolio needs.

**ESSENTIAL FUNCTIONS OF THE ROLE**
-----------------------------------

### **AI Use Case Data Science Delivery**

* Translate AI use-case objectives into data science problem statements, modeling approaches, analytical plans, success metrics, and execution roadmaps.
* Develop predictive models, classification models, segmentation approaches, personalization methods, statistical analyses, causal inference approaches, optimization models, simulations, or other traditional data science methods, and combine them with LLM- and agent-based approaches when appropriate to support AI use cases.
* Partner with product, engineering, data, ontology, and clinical/operational stakeholders to ensure data science work is aligned to real workflow needs and measurable outcomes.
* Rapidly prototype, validate, iterate, and productionalize data science, generative AI, and agentic methods in partnership with engineering and platform teams, with a bias toward delivering working capabilities into real user workflows.

The Children’s Tumor Foundation (CTF) is not a traditional research foundation. We operate as a patient-centered drug discovery engine for NF, a group of genetic conditions that cause tumors to grow on nerves affecting 1 in 2,000 individuals. We operate by accelerating the full continuum of scientific discovery, from basic research through translation to clinical trials and approved treatments — while empowering patients and building the financial infrastructure to support that journey. We catalyze progress by uniting academia, industry, regulators, and patient advocates around shared goals.

**General Summary**

The Biomedical Data Scientist will drive CTF’s efforts to turn neurofibromatosis (NF) data into actionable insights for drug discovery, positioning the Foundation as a leader in NF data. Working closely with CTF’s Science teams, this role integrates research, clinical and publicly available data to identify and prioritize therapeutic opportunities across NF1, *NF2*-related schwannomatosis, and non *NF2*-related schwannomatosis. The Biomedical Data Scientist will also work closely with vendors to steward CTF’s NF data ecosystem, lead CTF’s AI-enabled research resource for the NF community, and share data and findings with the broader research community. title: Associate Applied AI - Deep Learning/Time Series
description:
**Job Description**

**WHAT WE DO:**

At Goldman Sachs, our Engineers don't just make things – we make things possible. Change the world by connecting people and capital with ideas. Solve the most challenging and pressing engineering problems for our clients. Join our engineering teams that build massively scalable software and systems, architect low latency infrastructure solutions, proactively guard against cyber threats, and leverage machine learning alongside financial engineering to continuously turn data into action. Create new businesses, transform finance, and explore a world of opportunity at the speed of markets.

Engineering, which is comprised of our Technology Division and global strategists groups, is at the critical center of our business, and our dynamic environment requires innovative strategic thinking and immediate, real solutions. Want to push the limit of digital possibilities? Start here.

**AI RESEARCH AT GOLDMAN SACHS:**

The AI Research group is the firm's dedicated research organization, operating at the intersection of frontier machine learning and quantitative finance. We build, train, and rigorously evaluate deep learning models on some of the richest financial time series data in the industry — market microstructure, cross-asset pricing, macroeconomic indicators, transaction flows, and alternative data.

Our mandate is to advance the state of the art in sequence modelling and probabilistic forecasting for noisy, non-stationary, low signal-to-noise financial data, and to deliver that research as a firmwide platform that quantitative researchers, strategists, and engineering teams across the organization can build on. We operate with research rigor and engineering discipline — every model we ship is reproducible, benchmarked against strong baselines, and evaluated under realistic out-of-sample and out-of-regime conditions.

**THE ROLE:**

**Title:** AI Research – Associate **Location****:** New York, NY **Division****:** Engineering – AI Research

We are seeking a deeply hands-on researcher to lead the design, training, and evaluation of deep learning models for financial time series. This is an individual contributor role for someone who is equally comfortable deriving a likelihood, writing a distributed training loop across a multi-node GPU cluster, and defending an evaluation methodology to a room of quantitative researchers.

You will own research problems end to end: framing the question, curating and engineering the data, designing the model architecture, running large-scale training experiments, building the evaluation harness, and partnering with quant and engineering teams to bring models into production. Because our output serves multiple desks and asset classes, you will be expected to build models and abstractions that generalize — not one-off solutions.

This is a fast-moving research space. You thrive in ambiguity, you are skeptical of results that look too good, and you bring the same rigor to evaluation methodology that you bring to model design.

**WHAT YOU WILL BE WORKING ON:**

* **Model research and development:** Design, implement, and train modern deep learning architectures for forecasting, representation learning, and generative modelling of financial time series — including CNNs and temporal convolutional networks, Transformers and attention-based sequence models, autoencoders, GANs, diffusion models, graph neural networks, Bayesian networks, and reinforcement learning.

* **Time series specialization:** Build and benchmark against specialized sequence architectures including WaveNet, N-BEATS / N-HiTS, DeepAR, PatchTST, and Time Series Foundation Models (TSFMs), and rigorously baseline them against classical econometric methods such as ARIMA, GARCH, Kalman filters, and state space models.

**Required**

* A Bachelor's, Master's, or Ph.D. degree in Computer Science, Machine Learning, Statistics, Mathematics, Physics, Electrical Engineering, Quantitative Finance, or a related quantitative discipline.

* A minimum of 3+ years of industry experience building, training, and deploying deep learning models, with a substantial portion focused on sequential or time series data. Candidates with a Ph.D. and fewer years of industry experience will be considered where the depth of research experience is demonstrably equivalent.

* Deep expertise across modern deep learning architectures: CNNs and TCNs, Transformers, autoencoders, GANs, diffusion models, GNNs, Bayesian methods, and reinforcement learning.

* Strong working knowledge of classical time series and econometric modelling — ARIMA, GARCH, Kalman filtering, state space models — and clear judgment on when deep learning does and does not beat them.

* Practical experience with modern time series architectures such as WaveNet, N-BEATS / N-HiTS, DeepAR, PatchTST, or Time Series Foundation Models.

* Expert-level Python and deep proficiency in PyTorch, TensorFlow / Keras and/or JAX / Flax.

* Demonstrated experience with distributed and accelerated training (DDP, FSDP, multi-node GPU training) and model export and optimization workflows including ONNX.

* Rigorous foundations in statistics, probability, stochastic processes, optimization, and signal processing.

* Excellent oral and written communication skills, with the ability to articulate research trade-offs to both PhD researchers and non-technical business stakeholders.

* Comfort operating in a quickly evolving environment with a high degree of ambiguity and rapid change.

**Preferred**

* Prior machine learning or data science experience at a hedge fund, asset manager, proprietary trading firm, or systematic trading desk.

* Experience across multiple asset classes — equities, fixed income, FX, commodities, or multi-asset.

* Familiarity with Bayesian deep learning, probabilistic programming, or conformal prediction for uncertainty quantification.

* Experience with cloud platforms and containerized training environments (AWS, Kubernetes, Docker).

* Exposure to model risk management or regulatory frameworks in financial services.

* Contributions to open-source machine learning or time series libraries.

* Access to proprietary, high-quality cross-asset financial datasets at a scale few institutions can offer, and GPU compute to model them properly.

* Join a standalone research group that values rigor — strong baselines, rigorous evaluation, and reproducibility.

* Develop deep expertise at the intersection of frontier deep learning and quantitative finance, with the scope to shape the firm's applied AI research agenda.
