title: Statistician - School of Public Health (Austin)
description:
We are hiring a Statistician (Full-time) to join UTHealth Houston School of Public Health in Austin, TX. In this role, you will be responsible for becoming familiar with the databases and the coding already available, classifying the polypharmacy medications and comorbidities in the Medicare data to be summarized at the center level for the outcomes of interest. S/he will help with the transformation of the databases needed for each outcome detailed in the specific aims, as well as the subpopulation analyses proposed in the study (e.g., sex as a biological variable, race/ethnicity and quartiles of the social deprivation score). S/he will correctly link, across time, the datasets from the organizational aspects of each site from the intervention with the created datasets from the Medicare datasets to be able to examine the aims of the intervention at the center level. S/he will identify inconsistencies, narrow down the inclusion/exclusion criteria of participants for the secondary analysis under Dr. Pérez’s supervision after the data has been linked. Ideal candidate for this role should have a Bachelor’s degree and 2 years of experience. Proficiency in SAS software, EndNote, and Medicare data is preferred.

**What we do here changes the world.** UTHealth Houston is Texas’ resource for healthcare education, innovation, scientific discovery, and excellence in patient care. That’s where you come in.

**Once you join us you won't want to leave.** It’s because we reward our team for the excellent service they provide. Our total rewards package includes the benefits you’d expect from a top healthcare organization (benefits, insurance, etc.), plus:

* 100% paid medical premiums for our full-time employees
* Generous time off (holidays, preventative leave day, both vacation and sick time – all of which equates to around 37-38 days per year)
* The longer you stay, the more vacation you’ll accrue!
* Longevity Pay (Monthly payments after two years of service)
* Build your future with our awesome retirement/pension plan!

**We take care of our employees!** As a world-renowned institution, our employees’ wellbeing is important to us. We offer work/life services such as...

* Free financial and legal counseling
* Free mental health counseling services
* Gym membership discounts and access to wellness programs
* Other employee discounts including entertainment, car rentals, cell phones, etc.
* Resources for child and elder care
* Plus many more!

**Position Summary:**

This full-time statistician position is expected to join the project entitled “Leveraging a Natural Experiment to Determine the Effects of Integrated Palliative Care on Health Service Outcomes and Disparities in Parkinson Disease and Lewy Body Dementia”. The statistician will be responsible for becoming familiar with the databases and the existing SAS coding, classifying polypharmacy medications, end-of-life estimates, and comorbidities in the Medicare data to estimate the change between the pre-intervention 2019 and post-intervention 2024 measures. S/he will help with the transformation of the databases needed for each outcome on the 2024 datasets under the supervision of Dr. Pérez. S/he will correctly link, over time, the organizational datasets for each site in the intervention with the created Medicare datasets to examine the intervention's aims at the center level. S/he will identify inconsistencies in the 2024 post-intervention datasets for the secondary analysis under Dr. Pérez’s supervision after the data has been linked. S/he will learn to check and conduct the statistical analyses for handling missing data with Dr Pérez training. Afterward, this Statistician, with Dr. Pérez’s help, will explore the proposed associations and test the proposed hypothesis. Dr. Pérez and this Statistician will meet day-to-day to quickly set up, understand the challenges of these databases, and organize them to address the specific aims proposed. S/he will meet with Dr. Pérez in the weekly team meeting to move forward with the secondary data analyses to ensure that all the statistical analyses are scientifically sound. The statistician will help to create the tables and figures for manuscripts. The statistician will help write up the manuscripts for dissemination of study findings. Responsible for the application of standard statistical methods for conducting analysis and preparing reports.

Funding is expected to be received on October 17/2026 and it is expected to end on July 31/2028 after a renewal to be known on July 31/2027.

**Position Key Accountabilities:**

* Conducts data management of Medicare data in preparation for statistical analyses and reports.
* Supervises the routing tabulation of data; edits and analyzes the final material in the form of reports and records, including detail and summary tables, graphs, and charts.
* Performs statistical analyses from both large and small samples of data.
* Calculates medians quantities, percentiles, and coefficients of correlation.
* Tests data for sampling errors and for significance differences between samples.
* Performs other duties as assigned including literature reviews, formatting of tables, figures and manuscripts, mandatory trainings, etc.

**Certification/Skills:**

* Excellent communication skills both written and verbal.
* Working knowledge of MS Office.
* Proficiency in SAS software programming.
* Experience with Endnote, and Medicare data is a plus

**Minimum Education:**

* Bachelor's Degree in related field required

**Minimum Experience:**

* 2 years of experience in analysis and presentation of statistical data required May substitute required experience with equivalent years of education beyond the minimum education requirement.

**Physical Requirements:**

Exerts up to 20 pounds of force occasionally and/or up to 10 pounds frequently and/or a negligible amount constantly to move objects.

The school has vibrant undergraduate and graduate programs, with over 400 undergraduate majors and 170 graduate students, and an extensive research portfolio. Its faculty, staff, and students participate in a range of dynamic and collaborative research programs and enjoy modern facilities located on a pleasant urban campus in the City of Atlanta, Georgia. For more information on the school, visit https://chemistry.gatech.edu./

**Job Summary**
---------------

  

The School of Chemistry and Biochemistry at the Georgia Institute of Technology invites applications for a Research Scientist I position within the research group of Professor Facundo Fernández. The successful candidate will advance the CCSP collision cross section prediction platform, with a focus on developing, validating, and extending machine learning models that predict ion mobility collision cross section values directly from molecular structure. The role involves training and benchmarking gradient-boosted and graph-based models on large curated mass spectrometry datasets, including the METLIN-CCS database, and contributing to the public release of predictive tools used across metabolomics and lipidomics. This is a research-intensive position well suited to a candidate with strong computational skills and a working knowledge of analytical mass spectrometry.

**Responsibilities**
--------------------

  

Develop, train, and validate machine learning models, including gradient-boosted decision trees and graph-based architectures, to predict collision cross section values from molecular structure.

Curate, clean, and de-duplicate large collision cross section datasets, including the METLIN-CCS database, and generate molecular descriptors using RDKit and Mordred.

Design and execute rigorous benchmarking studies, including multi-seed reproducibility analysis and fair comparison against existing predictors retrained on common data splits.

Diagnose and resolve model performance issues such as overfitting and residual structure, and implement appropriate regularization and uncertainty quantification.

Extend the prediction framework to additional compound classes, including lipids, and contribute to documentation and public release of the platform.

Prepare figures, draft manuscripts, and present results at group meetings and scientific conferences.

The ability to communicate results clearly in writing and in oral presentations.

CNA is hiring for a Research Scientist to join their Data Science for Defense Production Systems Program. 1. Routinely produces analysis on structured and unstructured problems that meets CNA’s quality standards with limited direction and general supervision. Demonstrates ability to develop and apply creative and innovative analytic solutions to complex problems with assistance/support from more senior staff. Shows the ability to synthesize analytic results into a broader context. Can lead complex analytic projects with supervision. Begins to make connections and synthesize ideas across multiple, related studies.
  
  
2. Develops and maintains deep, specific institutional knowledge and expertise of primary clients/sponsors; their culture, organization, and issues. Uses that knowledge to support training & mentoring of new staff, to support on-going work, and to support development and shaping of new work for existing clients/ sponsors.
  
  
3. Balances responsiveness to guidance with independent action. Contributes productively and harmoniously to the work of others; treats everyone respectfully, professionally and fairly. Independently identifies opportunities for collaboration within team, division, and operating unit. Supports supervisor's initiatives and helps make vision a reality. Recognizes and acknowledges contributions from subordinates.
  
  
4. Supports business development efforts and/or marketing activities by interacting with CNA managers and current clients/sponsors on securing follow on work (e.g., small grants, or above core projects), expanding or developing new ideas for future projects, and occasionally working with potential clients/sponsors on developing new project ideas. Occasionally serves as internal reviewer of technical proposals.
  
  
5. Interacts regularly and independently with clients/sponsors and related parties. Typical interactions are at the "peer equivalent" level, but some level of interaction at senior level. Can effectively represent CNA as an organization.
  
  
6. Influences decisions by sponsors/ clients; provide sponsors/clients with implementable recommendations. Occasionally supports efforts to enhance CNA's reputation via publishing and outreach activities.
  
  
7. Demonstrates strong and effective communications skills, to include ability to summarize and synthesize larger pieces of work into effective executive summaries/executive briefings. Can effectively present work to more senior and larger audiences. Effectively communicates with & engages colleagues at all levels of the organization.
  
  
8. Works under limited direction and general supervision from division management. Can lead projects of low to medium size and/or complexity, as well as significant tasks on large or more complex projects. Effectively manages all aspects of assigned projects, to include delivery of high-quality analytic products on-time, and on-budget.
  
  
9. Plays a supporting role in the mentoring and training of new staff individually or as a member of a project team. Regularly demonstrates initiative in pursuing improvements in the quality of our projects and analytic products. Participates in corporate initiatives when asked to do so, and makes contributions to initiatives focused on making CNA a better place to work.
  
  
10. Performs other duties as assigned.
  
JOB REQUIREMENTS
  
**1. Education:** Minimum Master’s degree in a relevant field or equivalent experience, PhD preferred. Preference for applicants with backgrounds in operations research, industrial engineering, management science, systems engineering, data science, statistics, or quantitative/computational social sciences
  
  
**2. Experience:** Typical minimum requirements 5+ years of experience in research and analysis. Requires experience in R, Python, or other similar programming language. Experience with interactive visualizations, graphical users interfaces, and modeling and simulation preferred.
  
  
**3. Skills:**  

* Ability to work on progressively more difficult projects/analyses, including directing portions of large research projects or small to medium projects under general supervision
* Ability to operate independently and proactively in the execution of assignments
* Ability to work in a multi-disciplinary environment
* Strong critical thinking skills
* Knowledge of research techniques
* Strong planning and organizational skills
* Excellent interpersonal skills
* Strong and effective oral and written communication skills
* Ability to interact directly and effectively with clients and influence their decisions.

3. Writing Sample - Please upload a research paper or journal article that demonstrates your writing and research skills (draft copies are acceptable).
  
Optional documents

description:
**About Us**

The Colorado Rockies Baseball Club is embracing the climb, committed to building a championship-caliber organization on the field, in the clubhouse, and throughout our business operations. Playing at altitude presents unique competitive challenges and opportunities, and we embrace innovation, collaboration, and evidence-based practices to support elite performance.

Rooted in the traditions of America’s pastime, we operate with integrity, service, quality, and trust while striving to create an exceptional experience for our players, staff, and fans.

Our Baseball Analytics group partners with coaches, scouts, player development staff, medical and performance staff, and front office decision-makers to ask better questions, build better tools, and turn evidence into action.

**Position Summary**

The Colorado Rockies are seeking a senior-level analyst to join Baseball Analytics with a focus on developing and deploying predictive models and forecasts. The right candidate will combine technical rigor, baseball curiosity, and clear communication to help the organization make better decisions.

This posting may be filled at either the Senior Analyst or Lead Analyst level depending on the selected candidate’s experience, demonstrated ownership, and expected scope of responsibility.

The person in this role will help turn baseball questions into rigorous analysis, deployed predictive models, durable forecasting tools, and clear recommendations for Baseball Operations staff.

**Essential Duties & Responsibilities**

**Ready to Lead – Senior or Lead Analyst**

* Building, testing, documenting, and deploying predictive models and forecasts with a high degree of autonomy in determining model type, specification, and output.
* Communicating findings, uncertainty, and practical implications to Baseball Analytics colleagues and front office decisionmakers.
* Working with the team to identify forecasting questions worth testing and to turn successful analyses into work that can be repeated or handed off.

**Ready to Contribute**

* Contributing to a department-wide set of technical standards and project philosophy.
* Evaluating new research, data sources, technologies, and analytical methods for potential use in Baseball Operations.
* Collaborating with Baseball Systems, scouting, and player development groups to meet operational needs related to Baseball Analytics.

**Ready to Learn**

* Translating strong individual projects into repeatable systems, organizational best practices, and operational infrastructure.
* Learning the Rockies’ existing data, models, systems, and baseball workflows, with hands-on guidance during onboarding.
* Learning how to leverage predictive models in additional Baseball Operations workflows.
* Balancing immediate decision support with longer-term research and infrastructure investments.

**Additional Scope for a Lead Analyst**

* Helping coordinate forecasting research across the team, including organizing research discussions, reviewing others’ code, and advancing technical practices.
* Mentoring junior staff in Baseball Analytics, especially on projects related to predictive modeling and forecasting.
* Taking independent ownership of broader forecasting work after becoming familiar with the Rockies’ data, systems, and priorities.

**What We Value**

* Reproducible work and honest communication, because we want team players who are committed to doing right by collaborators over being right.
* Respect for empirical baseball expertise from practitioners such as coaches, scouts, players, and staff across the organization.
* Curiosity about the unique challenges and opportunities of competing at altitude.
* Continuous improvement in technical and professional skills.

**Job Qualifications**

Candidates should generally have at least 4 years of relevant experience, with 6 or more years expected for consideration at Lead Analyst. Advanced degrees such as a research-based master’s degree or PhD may count for up to 2 years when the topic is closely related to the role.

* Experience owning complex analytical projects from scoping through delivery.
* Evidence that analytical work has informed a decision or improved a workflow, with clear baseball-relevant or operational impact.
* Strong technical judgment in model development, validation, reproducibility, and communication.
* Ability to communicate priorities, uncertainty, and tradeoffs with credibility across highly technical to nontechnical audiences.
* Experience developing, validating, and deploying predictive models or forecasts in applied decision-making environments.
* Strong practical ability with R or Python, SQL, reproducible workflows, and model evaluation.

For consideration at the Lead Analyst level, we would also look for evidence of:

* Leading applied analytical work across projects or stakeholders.
* Shaping project direction, reviewing others’ work, and mentoring analysts.
* Coordinating people and work to move research forward.

**Work Schedule & Location**

* This position is based onsite at Coors Field in Denver, Colorado
* Work is performed in a combination of office settings, indoor training facilities, laboratory/performance environments, and outdoor baseball environments.
* Occasional travel to Spring Training in Scottsdale, minor league affiliate locations, training complexes, and other organizational sites may be required.

**Physical Job Requirements**

* Ability to remain in a stationary position (sitting or standing) for extended periods while analyzing data and using computer systems.
* Frequent use of a computer, keyboard, and other office equipment.
* Ability to communicate effectively in person, by phone, and via electronic communication.
* Ability to move throughout office spaces, clubhouses, dugouts, batting cages, bullpens, and performance labs.
* Ability to observe and interpret visual information, including data visualizations, video analysis, and live on-field activity.
* May occasionally lift and/or move items up to 25 pounds (e.g., portable technology equipment, training devices).
* Ability to work in varying environmental conditions, including indoor facilities and outdoor weather conditions typical of baseball operations.

**Compensation & Benefits**

Annual Salary Range: Senior Analyst: $110,000–$140,000; Lead Analyst: $130,000–$150,000. This position may be filled at either level based on the selected candidate’s experience and the scope of responsibility they will assume. This is a regular-status, full-time, exempt position.

Benefits include but are not limited to Medical, Dental, Vision, 401(k) with employer match, generous vacation and holiday program, employee parking, employer-provided game tickets to home games, onsite fitness classes and experiences, employee discounts on merchandise, and so much more! All benefits are subject to eligibility requirements and the terms of official plan documents, which may be modified or amended at any given time.

title: Statistical Programmer
description:
Princeton, NJ

Full Time

Biostatistics & Data Science

Entry Level

  

SystImmune is a leading and well-funded clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company located in Bothell, WA and Princeton, NJ. It specializes in developing innovative cancer treatments using its established drug development platforms, focusing on bi-specific, multi-specific antibodies, and antibody-drug conjugates (ADCs). SystImmune has multiple assets in various stages of clinical trials for solid tumor and hematologic indications. Alongside ongoing clinical trials. SystImmune has a robust preclinical pipeline of potential cancer therapeutics in the discover and IND-enabling stages, representing cutting-edge biologics development. We offer an opportunity for you to learn and grow while making significant contributions to the company's success.
  
  
The Statistical Programmer will support statistical programming activities for clinical trials, including generating SDTM/ADaM datasets, tables, figures, and listings (TFLs). This role is ideal for someone early in their career who is eager to learn and grow in a fast-paced biotech environment with exposure to end-to-end clinical development.
  
  
*This position is Hybrid (3 days onsite minimum) in our Princeton, NJ office.*
  
  
**Responsibilities**

* Collaborate with biostatisticians and cross-functional study team members to deliver statistical analysis and reporting outputs in line with project timelines.
* Review study documents including statistical analysis plans (SAPs), CRFs, database specifications, and data transfer specifications.
* Create and/or review SDTM/ADaM mapping specifications and annotated CRFs (aCRFs).
* Generate and/or validate SDTM and ADaM datasets, including associated Define.xml and reviewer’s guides.
* Develop and validate tables, figures, and listings (TFLs) to support clinical study analyses, regulatory submissions, conferences, and publications.
* Assess the quality, integrity, and consistency of analysis datasets, including cross-study analyses where applicable.
* Develop SAS programs and macros to automate dataset generation and reporting deliverables.
* Contribute to process improvements and enhancements of the statistical programming environment.
* Participate in study team meetings and representing statistical programming in cross-functional discussions.
* Apply knowledge of clinical trial design, CDISC standards, and regulatory requirements while producing analysis datasets and outputs in compliance with SOPs and industry standards.

**Qualifications**

* Master’s degree or higher in Biostatistics, Statistics, Mathematics, or a related scientific discipline, with 0–2 years of experience in statistical programming within the pharmaceutical/biotech industry or a CRO.
* Proficiency in SAS programming, preferably with experience in a clinical trial environment.
* Working knowledge of CDISC standards (SDTM and ADaM).
* Hands-on experience in developing and validating SDTM and ADaM datasets, as well as statistical outputs (tables, figures, and listings).
* Prior experience or exposure to oncology studies is preferred.
* Strong analytical, problem-solving, and organizational skills.
* Effective communication and interpersonal skills, with the ability to work collaboratively in cross-functional teams.

**Compensation and Benefits:**
  
The expected base salary range for this position is $80,000 - $100,000 annually. Actual compensation will be based on a variety of factors, including but not limited to a candidate’s level qualifications, experience, and skills.
  
While most offers typically fall within the **low to mid-point** of the range, we may extend an offer toward the higher end for exceptional candidates whose background and expertise exceeds the requirements of the role.
  
  
**SystImmune is a leading and well-funded biotech company with a bright future. We offer an opportunity for you to learn and grow while making significant contributions to the company’s success. SystImmune offers a comprehensive benefits package including: 100% paid employee premiums for medical/dental/vision, also STD, LTD, a 401(k) plan with a 50% company match of up to 3% and a vesting schedule of only 5 years, 15 PTO days per year, sick leave, plus 11 paid holidays and MORE.**
  
  
**We offer an opportunity for you to learn and grow while making significant contributions to the company’s success.**
  
  
**SystImmune is an Equal Opportunity Employer. We welcome diverse talent and encourage all qualified applicants to apply.**

Ultimately, you’ll provide a deep understanding of the data, what it all means, and how it can be used.

  
  

Work with us as we use data science for good.

  
  

Join us. The world can’t wait.

description:
**Research Statistician II**

**College Board –** Learning & Assessment

**Location:** This is a remote role. Candidates who live near CB offices have the option of being fully remote or hybrid (Tuesday and Wednesday in office). All CB employees are required to occasionally travel to meet in person for business purposes.

**About the Team**

The SAT Psychometrics, Analytics and Research (SPAR) team, as part of the larger Psychometrics group at College Board, supports more than seven million students a year as they prepare for a successful transition to college and career. SPAR partners closely with the College Readiness Assessments — primarily the SAT Suite of Assessments — to ensure operational excellence and best-in-class measurement solutions. Our work ensures that students, educators, and other stakeholders can trust the data that informs the most important decisions of their academic lives.

**About the Opportunity**

As a Research Statistician on the SPAR team, you will be a core contributor to the operational infrastructure that keeps the SAT Suite of Assessments running accurately and on schedule. This is a hands-on, production-oriented role that demands strong statistical programming skills, sound analytical judgment, and the ability to execute independently on time-sensitive work in a fast-moving environment.

Your primary work will span multiple critical operational pipelines. Each pipeline has defined deliverables, hard deadlines, and downstream dependencies — which means your ability to work independently, flag issues early, and move quickly through ambiguity matters as much as your technical skill. You will also contribute to process improvement initiatives and non-routine psychometric projects that strengthen the team's tools and capabilities over time.

This role is best suited for someone who takes ownership of their work— who initiates solutions rather than waiting to be guided, communicates proactively when conditions change, and holds themselves to a high standard of accuracy under time pressure.

**In This Role, You Will**

**Operational Data and Psychometric Support (50%)**

* Execute pretesting analyses for SAT Suite Administrations, including data extraction, classical item analysis and item response theory (IRT) analysis
* Execute psychometric maintenance analyses on the SAT Suite scores by a defined cycle, including data extraction, generation and QC of statistical reports
* Own compilation and quality control of assigned sections of client-facing technical analysis reports, ensuring review-ready accuracy for routine and ad hoc delivery to stakeholders
* Own compilation and quality control of assigned sections of client-facing technical analysis reports, ensuring review-ready accuracy for routine and ad hoc delivery to stakeholders

**Process and Tool Development (30%)**

* Independently develop, maintain, and update data management and statistical analysis code for operational processes
* Identify and implement improvements to existing operational workflows
* Contribute to the evaluation and adoption of Python-based solutions and other tools that improve team efficiency, scalability, and integration with organizational systems
* Maintain accurate and current documentation of processes, tools, and quality control findings to enhance team knowledge and operational continuity

**Collaboration and Communication (20%)**

* Partner with psychometricians, test development, technology, and other cross-functional teams to support accurate and timely delivery of assessment data and reports
* Represent SPAR's analytical work with accuracy and clarity in cross-functional discussions and project meetings
* Proactively manage work scope and status, identify blockers, and escalate issues in timely and appropriate manner

**About You**

To qualify for this role, you must have:

* Bachelor's or graduate degree in statistics, mathematics, psychometrics, or a related quantitative field
* 5–7 years of relevant experience in statistical programming, data analysis, or psychometric operations in a production or operational setting
* Proficiency in Python and R required and SAS a plus — including independent development and maintenance of complex projects in those languages
* Experience with Microsoft Office programs (Word, Excel, Access, PowerPoint, and Outlook) with an emphasis on MS Word and Excel
* Ability or willingness to leverage AI tools — including large language models, code generation assistants, and AI-enabled data workflows — to identify solution, improve productivity, and accelerate work delivery
* Demonstrated ability to work independently and to manage time-sensitive deliverables with urgency and accuracy
* Strong attention to detail with a consistent record of delivering accurate, error-free work in high-stakes operational contexts with downstream dependencies
* Ability to identify and flag issues early in a workflow
* Experience with psychometrics, educational measurement, or the standardized testing industry required; familiarity with item analysis, calibration, and scaling is a plus
* Experience with other advanced statistical or psychometric software preferred
* Excellent organizational and time management skills; demonstrated ability to manage multiple competing priorities simultaneously and adjust sequencing when needed
* Ability to travel 2–4 times per year to College Board offices or on behalf of College Board business

**All roles at College Board require:**

* A passion for expanding educational and career opportunities and mission-driven work
* Curiosity and enthusiasm for emerging technologies, with a willingness to experiment with and adopt new AI-driven solutions and comfort with learning and applying new digital tools independently and proactively.

description:
**JOB SUMMARY:**

NORC at the University of Chicago is seeking a qualified Data Analyst I or II (we are open to hiring at either level) to join the Statistics and Data Science department and support a diverse range of research projects. At NORC, Data Analysts are early career team members who train and work with our Statisticians and Data Scientists to perform tasks such as data processing, quality assurance, analysis, and dissemination.

As part of their data processing responsibilities, Data Analysts import, clean, standardize, transform, and validate data sets. They also research and document data procedures and support the investigation of data problems. They may identify, analyze, and interpret trends or patterns in data sets, support modeling efforts, and help prepare data presentations and reports, including developing charts, graphs, and tables. In addition, the Data Analyst may assist in data collection and harmonization from primary or secondary data sources (e.g., administrative records, commercial data, social media data), preparing data files for delivery, and the maintenance of databases, data systems, and their relevant metadata/dictionaries. The Data Analyst is expected to work collaboratively in a team environment.

*Qualified applicants must be eligible to work in the U.S. We regret that we are unable to offer visa sponsorship for this position.*

**Location**: This is a hybrid role based in either our Chicago Loop or downtown DC office, with a minimum of six days per month in the office.

*We welcome interest from future graduates; however, this position requires a completed Bachelor's degree. If you are still pursuing your degree, please consider applying once your graduation requirements have been met.*

  

**DEPARTMENT: Statistics and Data Science**

The Statistics and Data Science (SDS) department provides the scientific foundation required to advance NORC’s project portfolio. SDS delivers rigorous, innovative, and fit-for-purpose solutions along the project lifecycle. The department provides leadership for NORC’s approach on a broad range of approaches for study design and the analysis of primary and secondary data. SDS expertise includes artificial intelligence and machine learning; Bayesian analysis; causal inference; disclosure avoidance; imputation; data linkage and statistical matching for combining multiple data sources; data quality assessment; efficient and reproducible workflow development; privacy-preserving methods; small area estimation; statistical methods for survey sampling, weighting, estimation, and inference; and visualization.

The SDS department works closely with research, technology, and operational teams across NORC to ensure that statistical excellence and innovation remain central to the organization’s work. Many of NORC’s projects and proposals are led by substantive research departments that require significant contributions from SDS staff. SDS works closely with highly collaborative groups across the organization to ensure success through cross-departmental partnerships. To further capture the innovative spirit of NORC, SDS also leads projects that target departmental focus areas. Examples of recent project topics involving SDS staff include survey design, weighting, and analysis; AI for enhancing data quality, standardization, and integration; enhancing traffic safety data; linkage of health administrative data and surveys; and testing data visualization approaches for effective communication.

  

**RESPONSIBILITIES:**

* Collaborate with statisticians, data scientists, technology experts, and subject matter experts to implement and improve data management and analysis activities.
* Develop programs and scripts for data cleaning, integration, transformation, and harmonization, as well as data quality checks and validation
* Support and enhance applications and databases already built for various research needs and produce data documentation and dictionaries.
* Create data dashboards and visualizations, including preparing charts, graphs, and tables for reports and presentations.
* Perform various types of data analysis and modeling, often involving multiple data sets.
* Contribute to documentation, reports, and presentations through writing sections, creating basic analytic summaries, and developing tables and graphics.
* Apply AI tools to help improve efficiency.
* Perform other duties as assigned.

  

**REQUIRED SKILLS:**

* Bachelor’s degree in statistics, data science, computer science, or an equivalent field.
* 0-2 years’ relevant experience (internships included).
* Statistical programming in multiple packages and databases, including Python (required)
* Familiarity working with large data sets, conducting statistical and quantitative modeling with strong programming.
* Strong foundation in areas of analytic methods, data engineering, machine learning, and scientific methods of inquiry.
* Experience with data management, data reduction techniques and data visualization.
* Working knowledge of different types of data that can be sourced whether from administrative data, surveys, social media, or sensor data.
* Strong skills in problem solving and quantitative analysis are required, including a willingness to understand deviations and ask questions about data issues.
* Able to organize and prioritize work assignments to meet project needs.
* Strong communication, writing and data storytelling skills.
* Enthusiasm for teamwork and collaboration across disciplinary boundaries.

**Preferred Skills:**

* Experience working with SAS, Tableau, Hadoop, Hive, Databricks, MapReduce, and/or other large data systems
* Additional expertise in large and small language models, and machine learning, in working in cloud environments (e.g., AWS, Azure, GCP), and with command-line workflows (e.g., in bash)
* Experience with JavaScript programming.

*Qualified applicants must be eligible to work in the U.S. now and in the future. We regret that we are unable to offer visa sponsorship for this position.*

**Please include a Resume and Cover Letter when applying. Candidates should be prepared to provide professional references upon request.**

  

**SALARY AND BENEFITS:**

The pay range for this position is $62,000-$73,000.

This position is classified as regular. Regular staff are eligible for NORC’s comprehensive benefits program. Benefits include, but are not limited to:

* Generously subsidized health insurance, effective on the first day of employment
* Dental and vision insurance
* A defined contribution retirement program, along with a separate voluntary 403(b) retirement program
* Group life insurance, long-term and short-term disability insurance
* Benefits that promote work/life balance, including generous paid time off, holidays; paid parental leave, bereavement leave, tuition assistance, and an Employee Assistance Program (EAP).

*NORC is committed to equity and transparency in its pay practices. We publish salary ranges and benefit information for every job. The listed hiring range reflects what we, in good faith, expect to pay at the time of posting, though actual compensation may vary and may be adjusted over time. A candidate’s placement within the range depends on factors such as competencies, education, qualifications, experience, skills, performance, and organizational needs.*

  

**WHAT WE DO:**

NORC at the University of Chicago is an objective, non-partisan research institution that delivers reliable data and rigorous analysis to guide critical programmatic, business, and policy decisions. Since 1941, our teams have conducted groundbreaking studies, created and applied innovative methods and tools, and advanced principles of scientific integrity and collaboration. Today, government, corporate, and nonprofit clients around the world partner with us to transform increasingly complex information into useful knowledge.

  

**WHO WE ARE:**

For over 80 years, NORC has evolved in many ways, moving the needle with research methods, technical applications and groundbreaking research findings. But our tradition of excellence, passion for innovation, and commitment to collegiality have remained constant components of who we are as a brand, and who each of us is as a member of the NORC team. With world-class benefits, a business casual environment, and an emphasis on continuous learning, NORC is a place where people join for the stellar research and analysis work for which we’re known, and stay for the relationships they form with their colleagues who take pride in the impact their work is making on a global scale.

description:
### **About Hipcamp**

Over the past decade, Hipcamp has unlocked access to 5 million acres of private camping around the world. In addition to hosting over 120k campsites you won’t find anywhere else, Hipcamp also has the best collection of bookable tent, RV and cabin sites for all camping styles. Each year, Hipcamp helps millions of people happily sleep under the stars, boosting local economies and biodiversity along the way. Everything we do is guided by our belief that getting outside is good for the health of people and the environment. Our culture is built on a deep and genuine commitment to helping people connect with the outdoors. Hipcamp is also backed by top tier investors including Andreesen Horowitz, Benchmark, Bond Capital and Index Ventures.

**About the role**
------------------

We're looking for a Product Data Scientist to join our Analytics team, whose mission is to provide data insights that drive impact and guide strategy. You'll embed on the Host Camp, a small, cross-functional crew that spans across Product and Ops, to deeply understand the problems our Hosts face. You'll partner closely with team leads on strategy, dig into how people actually use Hipcamp to find growth opportunities, and make sure the team is investing in the most impactful projects.

As one of two Analysts, the ownership area is large and the autonomy is real. You'll work independently and collaboratively in equal measure, wear a few hats, help set the path when it isn't drawn yet, and find the signal in the ambiguity. You don't wait for a perfectly scoped question and hand a chart back over the fence. Instead, you spot the opportunity, form the hypothesis, validate it quickly, and land the answer that the team can act on. The foundational work that helps the team is as exciting to you as the big, deep analytical projects.

We're also big believers in putting AI to work, and we want someone excited to fold it into how they analyze, automate, and think, and to help the whole team do the same. You use statistics and models to inform your analysis and to co-design better experiments. You're literate enough in ML to read a model, reason about what it's telling you, and ask sharp questions of the people who build them. Above all, you connect the numbers to the decision.

**What you'll do**
------------------

* Partner with Product and Ops to shape strategy for the Host Camp by uncovering growth opportunities, developing your own hypotheses, and making the analytical case for where the team should focus.
* Co-design experiments, using model outputs and statistical thinking to shape smarter tests that you then set up and iterate quickly to pressure-test your conclusions.
* Keep the Camp's key performance metrics visible and easy to reach, so everyone can see how they're doing.
* Use AI throughout your analytical workflow to accelerate exploration, automate repetitive work, prototype ideas quickly, and spend more time on high-value thinking.
* Partner with Data Engineering to build our AI-powered analytics platform, creating reusable workflows and self-service tools that make trusted data and insights easier to access across the company.

**What you'll bring**
---------------------

* 6+ years in product, growth, or marketing analytics or data science.
* Strong SQL and data visualization skills.
* Solid statistics. You design and read experiments well, reason about significance and causality, and know a real signal from noise.
* Enough ML literacy to use models well: you can interpret model output, fold it into analysis, and co-design experiments around it.
* A knack for storytelling and clear communication. You translate analysis into a decision, and move a team with it.
* Comfort in a fast-paced environment where priorities shift and you adapt as we learn. You're happy finding impact where the path isn't obvious yet.
* A full-stack way of working. You generate your own hypotheses, validate them pragmatically, and carry solutions through to implementation.
* Fluency with AI, and eagerness to weave it into how you (and the team) work.
* Ease working both independently and with a distributed, cross-functional team.
* Curiosity to deeply understand the community we serve.
* A real passion for our mission.

Don't check every box? Please apply anyway. Some of our best teammates came in a little outside the lines.

### **About our Work Environment**

Compensation will be a mix of salary and stock options. It will be highly competitive compared to similar-stage companies and based on location.

Health is essential to happiness. In addition to full health insurance, all team members receive $1K in Hipcash because we believe getting outside is excellent preventative medicine in addition to increasing your creativity, lowering your stress, and making you an overall more awesome human.

We focus on results, not hours. We believe that clearly defined goals combined with great people, empowerment, and autonomy create the best results. We feel confident that inclusive and diverse teams working on an important cause can accomplish extraordinary things.

Hipcamp is an equal opportunity employer and value diversity at our company. We do not discriminate on the basis of race, religion, color, national origin, gender, sexual orientation, age, marital status, veteran status, or disability status. In fact we are confident that the most inclusive and diverse teams accomplish the most extraordinary results.

Are you an experienced AI/ML engineer who thrives in a fast-paced environment, enjoys turning research and prototypes into real mission capability, and wants to help shape how AI is built and delivered across a national mission?

If so, then apply today and be part of a team that supports the United States Cyber Command (USCC). Our team is standing up USCYBERCOM's AI Enterprise capability - the central hub that mission teams turn to when they want to move an AI solution from prototype to a secure, governed, enterprise-scale service. As a Senior AI/ML Engineer on this team, you will design and integrate the models, agents, and AI workflows that run on that platform, with significant, visible impact on the mission of the USCC.

description:
##### **About Spokeo**

Spokeo is a people intelligence platform that helps over 18 million monthly visitors reconnect with friends, reunite with families, and build trust in new relationships. Thousands of companies also trust Spokeo's 60 billion public records to improve customer research, help verify information, and prevent fraud.

Founded in 2006, Spokeo has built a dedicated, remote-first team with an average tenure of 6.9 years. Comparably has recognized it as a Best Company for Compensation, Employee Happiness, Perks and Benefits, Support for Women, Work-Life Balance, and CEO Leadership.

##### **About This Opportunity**

Every Spokeo search result depends on one decision: do these records describe the same person, and how sure are we? You will build the models that make that call, on messy data from many vendors and public sources, where there is no answer key to check against.

You will own a modeling problem from the first question to the production release, and you will see your work change what customers see. The Data Science team is small, so you work directly with the Director of Data Science and the product owners. If you like designing the test as much as building the model, and you want to mentor teammates as the team grows, this is the place to do it.

##### **What You'll Do:**

Rough share of your time, subject to change.

* 35%: Build and improve the models that match records and score how confident we are in each result. You will choose the approach, train it, test it honestly on held-out data, and ship it.
* 20%: Design the labels and the measurement. Decide what to hand-check, build the evaluation sets, and estimate how often we are right when a full answer key does not exist. This includes using AI models to help label at scale, and checking them against human judgment.
* 15%: Take models to production on AWS, with ML engineering and DevOps. That covers the retrain schedule, the model registry, and a record of where every model and its data came from.
* 10%: Review each data build before it ships. Find what changed, catch regressions, and explain it in plain language to product and sales partners.
* 10%: Work with the Product Owner to turn findings into stories with clear targets, and defend the priority of the next research spike.
* 10%: Document your methods, review teammates' code, and take part in the DS/ML working group.

Tools. What you will work with: Python, SQL, Spark, AWS SageMaker, Databricks, and MLflow.

Challenges. Noisy and incomplete records, no large hand-labeled set to lean on, and opt-out and retention rules that every model must respect.

People. The Director of Data Science, product owners, ML engineers, DevOps, and the DS/ML working group.

##### **Who You Are:**

What you have done matters more than the tools you have touched. Equivalent experience counts.

* Required: 6+ years of applied data science, though what you have shipped matters more than the count.
* Required: A Bachelor’s degree in a quantitative field is expected, and a master’s is preferred, or equivalent professional experience.
* Taken a model from idea to production in a cloud setting (AWS SageMaker, Databricks, MLflow, or similar), monitored it, and measured how it performed after launch.
* Worked with very large datasets (100 million rows or more) using Spark or a similar tool, with Python and SQL.
* Judged whether a model is good when no clean answer key exists, for example by sampling and hand-checking results, and said how confident you are in the number.
* Told a real improvement from noise, and explained the result, its limits, and the tradeoffs in plain language to engineers and product owners alike.
* Kept a model healthy as its data changed: knowing when labels and models have gone out of date and need refreshing, and writing the process down so a teammate can pick it up.
* Handled personal data responsibly, following opt-out, retention, and lineage rules without being reminded.
* Experience matching or de-duplicating records, using AI to help label data, graph methods, or turning a raw model score into a confidence a product team can act on, is a plus.

Our mission is to advance transparency, and to achieve that goal, we rally around six core values: listening with empathy, understanding the why, clarifying with data, innovating to learn, collaborating to achieve, and insisting on quality.

KBR is seeking a full-time Geospatial Data Scientist to join its talented team in Sioux Falls, South Dakota. The successful candidate will become an integral part of the Land Processes Distributed Active Archive Center (LP DAAC, https://www.earthdata.nasa.gov/centers/lp-daac), a National Aeronautics and Space Administration (NASA)-funded project located at the USGS EROS Center. The LP DAAC operates as a partnership between the USGS and NASA and is a component of NASA’s Earth Observing System Data and Information System (EOSDIS). Geospatial data scientists, system engineers, user services representatives, and outreach staff work together to support LP DAAC activities and distribute data to the earth science community.

The Geospatial Data Scientist will utilize Geographic Information System (GIS) software and scripting techniques against a broad spectrum of remote sensing data, assessing their suitability for NASA’s Application for Extracting and Exploring Analysis Ready Samples (AppEEARS) and validating AppEEARS outputs against source data. The selected candidate will also work closely with science teams and data providers to understand user community needs, then develop science enablement materials that make it easier for those communities and users broadly to work with the data. The majority of the role is hands-on coding and analysis: writing SQL against a Snowflake data warehouse, building Python-based analytical models, and developing BI dashboards. **A Day in the Life**

* Write SQL and Python to build, test, and maintain analytical datasets and pipelines in Snowflake.
* Build descriptive analytics: dashboards, KPI frameworks, and ad hoc queries that answer "what happened and why."
* Build predictive models: forecasting, segmentation, and other statistical/ML models that answer "what's likely to happen."
* Build prescriptive analysis: scenario modeling and recommendations that answer "what should we do."
* Partner with Finance, Ops, Marketing, and Development stakeholders to scope analytical questions and translate business problems into data solutions.
* Design and maintain BI dashboards (Power BI, Omni) for self-serve reporting across teams.
* Conduct exploratory data analysis to surface trends, anomalies, and root causes in business performance.
* Present findings and recommendations clearly to both technical and non-technical audiences.

* Working knowledge of statistical and machine learning methods (regression, classification, clustering, time series forecasting) and when to apply them.
* Experience building and maintaining BI dashboards (Power BI, Looker, Tableau, or similar) for multiple business audiences.
* Ability to translate ambiguous business questions from Finance, Ops, Marketing, or Development into a defined analytical approach.

* Ability to thrive independently in a fast-paced, dynamic environment while managing multiple priorities.
* Strong communication skills, capable of explaining technical work to non-technical stakeholders.

**Education and Experience**

* Bachelor's degree in data science, statistics, computer science, or a related quantitative field.

description:
**About Airwallex**
-------------------

Airwallex is the AI-native financial operating system for a real-time, intelligent economy. More than 675,000 businesses, including McLaren Racing, Qantas, SHEIN, and TikTok, use us, directly or through our platform partners, to run their financial operations or build and monetize financial products of their own.

We started in Melbourne in 2015 to build the infrastructure global commerce runs on. We're the regulated backbone behind global payments: not by accident, but by design. A decade plus, 85+ licenses, and a financial infrastructure spanning North America, Europe, the Middle East, and Asia-Pacific.

We're co-headquartered in San Francisco and Singapore, with more than 2,700 people across 27 offices. We hire builders with founder-level energy, people who move fast with good judgment, dig in with real curiosity, and make calls from first principles rather than waiting to be told what to do. Read our operating principles to see it in full.

  

**How you'll make impact**
--------------------------

You’ll shape the next phase of Airwallex’s growth by building data science systems that improve how we acquire, activate, engage, retain, and expand customers globally.

* Design, deploy, and iterate on predictive models, personalization and recommendation systems, LLM-powered applications, incentive optimization frameworks, and causal inference models that drive measurable business outcomes.
* Partner with Growth, Marketing, Product, Sales, Engineering, and other cross-functional teams to turn data and AI into clear recommendations, stronger investment decisions, and effective go-to-market strategies.
* Measure the causal impact of marketing and growth initiatives, identify what’s working, and translate those findings into action.
* Raise the technical bar for the data science team through hands-on leadership, mentorship, and a clear vision for longer-term direction.

You’ll be based in San Francisco and work from the office three days a week.

**What we're looking for**
--------------------------

### **Essentials**

* 7+ years of industry experience and an advanced degree, such as a PhD or MS, in a quantitative field such as Statistics, Engineering, the Sciences, Computer Science, or Economics.
* Expert knowledge of machine learning and statistical modelling for data-driven growth strategy.
* Hands-on experience building, deploying, and maintaining machine learning models in production-grade systems, including cloud-based services and real-time or batch pipelines.
* Strong experience with data querying languages such as SQL and scripting languages such as Python.
* Experience applying machine learning and statistical models to measure the causal impact of marketing or growth initiatives.
* Strong experience in AI harness and building AI agents.

### **Preferred**

* Experience with schema design and dimensional data modelling.
* Experience communicating analysis and recommendations to leadership and cross-functional teams to influence strategy.
* Experience in technology, financial services, or a high-growth environment.
* Experience providing technical mentorship on machine learning and experimentation in an industry setting.

**You'll thrive here if**
-------------------------

* You're comfortable owning the roadmap yourself.
* You own the outcome and you don't wait for permission to fix what's broken.
* You're comfortable making decisions with incomplete information and moving quickly anyway.
* You're not precious about your ideas. You push hard for what you believe in, but you pivot fast when the data says otherwise.
* You connect dots across functions and hold the big picture without losing grip on the details.

**Learn more about your team**
------------------------------

Data Science at Airwallex is evolving from individual analyses and standalone models into scalable systems of decision and action. We bring together two complementary capabilities: DS Analytics, which improves decision quality and reduces decision latency, and DS Algorithm, which directly optimizes product and business outcomes in real time.

You’ll build systems of decision that help teams understand what changed, determine what to do next, and learn whether the action worked. This means owning the AI analytics harness around the analysis—including semantic layers, context retrieval, evaluation infrastructure, validation gates, and governance—so decisions remain reliable, contextualized, and trustworthy at scale.

You’ll also build systems of action that use machine learning and AI to shape product behavior, ranking, pricing, risk, allocation, and customer experiences. The work extends beyond training models to designing how intelligent systems reason, use tools, operate within guardrails, execute workflows, and measure their incremental impact.

As AI makes ad hoc analysis increasingly accessible, the remaining advantage is scale, scientific method, and rigor. You’ll structure ambiguous problems, design experiments, identify confounding factors, challenge misleading conclusions, and build production systems that produce reliable outcomes repeatedly—not just one-off answers.

The work is moving up the stack: from analysis to system, from model to harness, and from answering a question once to building something that answers it correctly over time. If you want to create data science systems that compound decision quality and turn intelligence into measurable action, this is where that work happens.

description:
### **Job Description:**

**Job Overview**
================

We are looking for an **Applied Scientist/Research Engineer** to improve the quality of training data and evaluation systems used to develop advanced AI models.

In this role, you will investigate how data quality, dataset composition, and evaluation methods influence model performance. You will design experiments, develop data curation and scoring methods, analyze model failures, and build tools that help us identify the data most valuable for training and improving AI systems.

This role is ideal for someone with a strong background in applied ML research, data-centric AI, or model evaluation who enjoys turning research insights into practical improvements.

**What You Will Own**
=====================

* Develop methods for training data curation, quality scoring, dataset selection, and data mixing.
* Design evaluation frameworks and benchmarks to measure model capabilities and identify performance gaps.
* Analyze model failures to understand how training data affects model behavior and generalization.
* Apply techniques such as active learning and human-in-the-loop evaluation to improve data efficiency and annotation quality.
* Build automated tools and pipelines to improve data quality while reducing annotation costs and manual effort.
* Design and run experiments to measure how data improvements translate into better model performance.
* Collaborate with research, engineering, and data operations teams to turn findings into scalable solutions.

* Experience in applied ML research, data science, AI evaluation, or a related technical field.
* Strong Python skills and experience with relevant ML frameworks and data processing tools.
* Experience with one or more of the following: training data curation, dataset optimization, model evaluation, benchmark development, active learning, or post-training.
* Strong experimental design and analytical skills, with the ability to connect data characteristics to model performance.
* Experience developing technical solutions, research methods, or automated pipelines rather than only performing annotation or data labeling.

description:

Machine Learning & AI Research

*The WHOOP compensation philosophy is designed to attract, motivate, and retain exceptional talent by offering competitive base salaries, meaningful equity, and consistent pay practices that reflect our mission and core values.*

  

*At WHOOP, we view total compensation as the combination of base salary, equity, and benefits, with equity serving as a key differentiator that aligns our employees with the long-term success of the company and allows every member of our corporate team to own part of WHOOP and share in the company’s long-term growth and success.*

  

*The U.S. base salary range for this full-time position is $170,000 - $230,000 Salary ranges are determined by role, level, and location. Within each range, individual pay is based on factors such as job-related skills, experience, performance, and relevant education or training.*

  

*In addition to the base salary, the successful candidate will also receive benefits and a generous equity package.*

  

*These ranges may be modified in the future to reflect evolving market conditions and organizational needs. While most offers will typically fall toward the starting point of the range, total compensation will depend on the candidate’s specific qualifications, expertise, and alignment with the role’s requirements.*

  

At WHOOP, we’re on a mission to unlock and inspire performance for life. WHOOP empowers members to perform at a higher level through a deeper understanding of their bodies and daily lives. Our wearable technology collects rich physiological data, providing members with actionable insights into their recovery, training, and sleep.

The Health team develops the algorithms and features that expand WHOOP's health sensing capabilities. The work spans women's health, software as a medical device, wellness and longevity, member insights, and emerging health signals. We combine continuous physiological data with clinical research and domain expertise to ship features that are scientifically grounded and useful to millions of members.

As a Staff Applied Machine Learning Scientist on the Health team, you will turn ambiguous clinical and product questions into defensible studies, models, and evaluation plans on WHOOP's longitudinal wearable and member data (physiological signals, behavioral logs, labs and integrations, and related streams). You will set the methodological bar for a Health domain. You will partner with Machine Learning Engineers on the path to production, and with Product, clinical, and Digital Health partners on what the data can and cannot support.

Success in this role requires applied algorithm and statistical craft, the judgment to operate across Health problem types, and Staff-level leadership: launching domain work independently, raising the quality and velocity of the people around you, and making clear prioritization calls under uncertainty.

### **Responsibilities**

* Lead the design, development, and validation of machine learning and statistical methods for Health features, using wearable physiological and behavioral data and related member sources.
* Frame ambiguous health and product questions into well-scoped modeling or study problems, with clear performance criteria, evaluation plans, and honest treatment of uncertainty and failure modes.
* Set the methodological and quality standard for a Health domain: reusable evaluation practices, review expectations, and documentation that others can inherit.
* Develop and refine approaches for time-series, longitudinal, and multimodal data, including data curation, labeling strategy, feature and representation choices, and offline evaluation that holds up under real-world noise, missingness, and population shift.
* Partner with Machine Learning Engineers to translate validated methods into production-ready systems, making modeling choices that account for scalability, reliability, latency, cost, monitoring, and (where relevant) controlled-release constraints.
* Serve as a technical counterpart to Product and Digital Health (clinical science, regulatory, quality): pressure-test performance requirements, study design, and evidence quality, and push back when a claim is not supportable.
* Raise the quality and velocity of the scientists and engineers around you through design reviews, mentorship, and the judgment of when to coach someone else to champion a problem versus taking it yourself.
* Communicate trade-offs, risks, and results clearly to technical, clinical, product, and leadership audiences; prevent misalignment early; drive decisions with evidence and a clear point of view on domain direction.

### **Qualifications**

* Master's or PhD (or equivalent professional experience) in Biomedical Engineering, Electrical Engineering, Computer Science, Applied Mathematics, Biostatistics, Bioinformatics, Physiology, or a related quantitative or health-science field.
* 7+ years of professional experience developing algorithms, applied ML models, or statistically rigorous analyses in health, wearables, medical devices, digital health, or a closely related domain.
* Demonstrated Staff-level technical leadership: setting methodological standards others reuse, influencing multi-team outcomes, mentoring senior ICs, and making prioritization calls under uncertainty. End-to-end project ownership alone is not sufficient.
* Strong foundation in statistics (Bayesian and frequentist) and machine learning for time-series and longitudinal data, with the ability to draw defensible conclusions from observational, noisy, or otherwise messy real-world data.
* Experience with wearable or physiological signals (PPG, IMU, HR/HRV, sleep, activity, temperature, or similar) or a closely related adjacent time-series domain.
* Hands-on experience designing studies or evaluation protocols end-to-end: data curation, metric choice, validation splits, subgroup and failure analysis, and documentation of assumptions and limitations.
* Strong Python skills with reproducible scientific / ML engineering hygiene (clean, reviewable code; comfort with stacks such as NumPy/SciPy/pandas, scikit-learn, PyTorch/TensorFlow).
* Clear, high-signal communicator who can move between deeply technical method discussions and cross-functional conversations with Product, clinical partners, and leadership.

***This role is based in the WHOOP office located in Boston, MA. The successful candidate must be prepared to relocate if necessary to work out of the Boston, MA office.***

  

*Interested in the role, but don’t meet every qualification? We encourage you to still apply! At WHOOP, we believe there is much more to a candidate than what is written on paper, and we value character as much as experience. As we continue to build a diverse and inclusive environment, we encourage anyone who is interested in this role to apply.*

  

*WHOOP is an Equal Opportunity Employer and participates in* *E-verify* *to determine employment eligibility. It is unlawful in Massachusetts to require or administer a lie detector test as a condition of employment or continued employment. An employer who violates this law shall be subject to criminal penalties and civil liability.*

description:
**About Care Access**

Care Access is working to make the future of health better for all. **With hundreds of research locations, mobile clinics, and clinicians across the globe, we bring world-class research and health services directly to communities that often face barriers to care.** We are dedicated to ensuring that every person has the opportunity to understand their health, access the care they need, **and contribute to the medical breakthroughs of tomorrow.**

With programs like *Future of Medicine*, which makes advanced health screenings and research opportunities accessible to communities worldwide, and *Difference Makers*, which supports local leaders to expand their community health and wellbeing efforts, we put people at the heart of medical progress. Through partnerships, technology, and perseverance, we are reimagining how clinical research and health services reach the world. Together, we are building a future of health that is better and more accessible for all.

To learn more about Care Access, visit www.CareAccess.com.

### **How This Role Makes a Difference**

As a **Senior Data Scientist**, you will play a pivotal role in advancing Reify Health's data-driven solutions for clinical trials. In this position, you will drive the development of statistical models and machine learning algorithms to improve patient enrollment and trial management. You'll work in a highly regulated healthcare data environment, ensuring compliance with privacy standards while innovating on predictive analytics. This role involves close collaboration with cross-functional teams (especially ML Engineering) to translate complex data insights into practical, impactful tools for the clinical research community.

### **How You'll Make An Impact**

* Site Randomization Forecasting: Develop/enhance forecasting models for site randomization and enrollment trends, enabling better planning and resource allocation across trial sites.
* Patient Matching/Ranking Algorithms: Support projects to build algorithms that intelligently match patients to (or rank patients for) appropriate clinical trials, enhancing recruitment efficiency and patient inclusion.
* Develop Other Advanced Statistical Models: Create and refine predictive models (Bayesian inference, regression analysis, time-series forecasting) to address other key clinical trial challenges and improve decision-making.
* AI Monitoring and Bias Detection: Implement processes to monitor machine learning models in production, detecting bias or performance drift and ensuring models remain fair, accurate, and compliant.
* Data Pipeline & Tooling Development: Build and optimize data pipelines and analytical workflows using tools like AWS Athena, Redshift, SageMaker, and dbt, enabling scalable model training and deployment.
* Regulatory Compliance in Data Science: Ensure all data science practices align with HIPAA, GDPR, and other privacy regulations, integrating compliance considerations into model development and data handling.
* Cross-Functional Collaboration: Work closely with machine learning engineers, product managers, and other stakeholders to integrate models into products and clearly communicate insights and recommendations.

### **The Expertise Required**

* Statistical & ML Expertise: Strong foundation in statistical modeling and machine learning techniques, including experience with Bayesian methods, regression analysis, and time-series forecasting.
* Model Monitoring & Fairness: Proficiency in evaluating model performance and bias, with the ability to implement AI monitoring tools and bias mitigation strategies to ensure ethical and reliable outcomes.
* Technical Toolset: Advanced programming skills in Python (with libraries such as scikit-learn, PyMC, mlforecast, etc.) and SQL, as well as familiarity with data transformation tools like dbt.
* Cloud & Data Infrastructure: Hands-on experience with cloud-based analytics and ML services, especially AWS tools (Athena for querying, Redshift for data warehousing, SageMaker for model development/deployment).
* Regulated Data Handling: Experience working with sensitive healthcare or clinical trial data under regulations like HIPAA and GDPR, demonstrating a deep commitment to data privacy and security best practices.
* Collaborative Communication: Excellent teamwork and meticulous verbal/written communication abilities, with a track record of partnering with engineering and product teams to translate data science work into actionable business solutions.
* Domain Knowledge: Understanding of clinical research or health-tech environments is highly valuable, including insight into clinical trial operations and a passion for improving patient outcomes through data.

### **Certifications/Licenses, Education, and Experience:**

* Minimum Education:
  + Minimum of Master's or Ph.D. in Statistics, Data Science, Computer Science, or a related quantitative field (or equivalent professional experience).
* Minimum Experience:
  + Minimum of 5+ years of hands-on data science or analytics experience, preferably in a healthcare, clinical research, or other highly regulated data environment.

### **How We Work Together**

* **Location**: Remote within the United States. This role requires 100% of work to be performed in a remote office environment.
* **Travel**: This is a remote position with less than 10% travel requirements. Occasional planned travel may be required as part of the role.

**Career Title:** Data Scientist, Test Security

**Department:** Measurement Services

**Salary:** Competitive salary commensurate with experience

**FLSA:** Exempt

**Note:** Union dues are 1.44% of bi-weekly pay

**Career Summary:**

The American Nurses Enterprise (ANE) is seeking a Data Scientist, Test Security to help safeguard the validity, integrity, and credibility of its certification programs. This role applies data forensics, advanced analytics, and investigative expertise to identify anomalies, assess security risks, and detect emerging trends. The Data Scientist manages the full data lifecycle by gathering, preparing, validating, and analyzing information from multiple systems and sources. In collaboration with cross-functional teams, this position leads initiatives that strengthen test security practices, improve operational processes, and enhance program effectiveness. The role also develops clear, meaningful reports, dashboards, and presentations that translate complex findings into actionable insights for strategic and operational decision-making.

Join the American Nurses Enterprise (ANE) and be part of the team building a healthy world through The Power of Nurses®. Our goals are to (1) Elevate the Profession of Nursing Globally

(2) Evolve the Practice of Nursing to Improve Health, Health Care, and Health Equity and (3) Ensure the Professional Success of Nurses. Our core values: Trusted, Inclusive, Innovative and Empowered guide everything we do. We are committed to creating a supportive and dynamic workplace where employees can thrive.

We understand the importance of work-life balance and offer flexible work arrangements and generous paid time off. Our modern office spaces are designed to foster collaboration and creativity. The collaborative culture and supportive team environment make ANE a great place to grow your career.

**What You Will Do:**

**Data Management, Quality & Analysis**

* Ensures data are accurate, reliable, and actionable to support operational and strategic initiatives.
* Collects, prepares, integrates, and validates data from multiple systems and sources.
* Monitors and maintains data quality standards, identifying and resolving inconsistencies or gaps.
* Performs exploratory and advanced analyses to identify trends, risks, opportunities, and business insights.
* Develops queries, data pipelines, and analytical processes that improve data accessibility and reliability.
* Establishes and maintains documentation related to data sources, definitions, methodologies,and processes.

**Test Security Analytics & Data Forensics**

* Protects the integrity of certification programs through data-driven detection and investigation of security risks.
* Analyzes examination and test taker data to identify patterns, anomalies, and indicators of potential misconduct or security threats.

description:
In the 1840s, Charles Babbage and Ada Lovelace worked on an early version of the computer known as the “Analytics Engine”. In the words of computing historian Doron Swade, “What Lovelace saw...was that numbers could represent entities other than quantity” and together they laid the foundation for general-purpose computing.

While much has changed since then, the importance of numbers in building great technology remains. We’re looking for Data Scientists who can help us build our analytics engine by making meaning from data and identifying opportunities for improvement.

As a Growth Data Scientist at Mercury, you will partner with Growth product, design, engineering and marketing leaders to shape how Mercury acquires, activates and retains customers across business and personal banking\*. This is a strategic, product-facing role: you’ll frame the “why” behind what we build, size opportunities, and turn the growth funnel into clear, prioritized recommendations. You will work as a full-stack Data Scientist on projects end to end and build deep domain expertise at the intersection of Data Science, Product and Growth. You will help set the direction for how Growth measures success and decides where to invest, in line with Mercury’s broader product and company goals.

* Partner with Growth product, design, engineering and marketing leaders to identify the highest-impact business questions, and influence what gets built and why.
